texto: C'est probablement l'un des pires Kubrick selon moi. Le film nous propose une sorte de huis clos politique qui ressemble plus à l'ancêtre de BFM TV qu'à un véritable film. Ça parle, ça reparle, ça rediscute encore et encore pour finalement pas grand-chose. Mais surtout, sans que le film ait réellement l'impression d'avancer. J'ai l'impression d'avoir entendu les mêmes discours pendant 1h30, le même message pendant 1h30, les mêmes phrases pendant 1h30 et surtout les mêmes dialogues répétitifs pendant 1h30. C'est clairement l'emploi du temps de BFM TV ! Les acteurs sont très limités, jusqu'à un point où un seul acteur joue trois personnages différents. C'est peut-être la seule véritable prouesse du film, mais malheureusement, même avec le maquillage, les costumes et les changements de personnage, on le reconnaît immédiatement. Ça devient presque ridicule. Le jeu d'acteur est souvent surjoué et mal dosé. Et surtout, l'humour noir et l'absurdité qu'on m'avait vendus sont quasiment absents. On m'avait vendu un film rempli d'humour noir, d'absurdité et de satire. Au final, j'ai trouvé une ou deux scènes réellement amusantes, mais le reste est beaucoup trop sérieux. Ce n'est même pas vraiment une comédie à mes yeux. L'absurdité apparaît peut-être une ou deux fois, puis disparaît complètement. L'humour noir qu'on m'avait promis s'est littéralement fait cracher dessus avant même d'arriver. Et décidément, un huis clos ne pourra jamais faire mieux que 12 Hommes en colère. La tension est artificielle, les rebondissements sont quasiment inexistants et, pendant 1h30, j'ai surtout eu l'impression de regarder un discours politique interminable. Je ne trouve quasiment rien de cinématographique ou de créatif dans ce film. À part une ou deux scènes rigolotes, il n'y a pas grand-chose qui m'a diverti. Et même la musique me paraît, selon moi, plus créative et plus complète que le film en entier. Elle propose davantage d'idées, d'ambiance et de variété que ce que le film arrive à me proposer pendant 1h30. C'est quand même assez ironique de sortir d'un film en ayant l'impression que sa bande-son est plus intéressante que son propre contenu. Mais il y a quand même quelques passages que j'ai trouvés vraiment réussis. Les séquences autour de la guerre, notamment tout ce qui concerne l'avion et son crash, sont particulièrement bien faites pour l'époque, surtout quand on prend en compte le budget du film. Visuellement, ces passages sont beaucoup plus intéressants et montrent enfin quelque chose de réellement cinématographique. Les indications militaires, le contexte de la guerre et tout ce qui touche à la menace communiste sont également plutôt sympathiques. Ces passages sont malheureusement assez rares, mais lorsqu'ils arrivent, ils m'ont presque permis de ne pas décrocher complètement. C'est peut-être même ce qui m'a empêché de passer mon temps à faire défiler une émission politique comme si je pouvais simplement scroller pour passer à la prochaine émission. Bref, un huis clos ultra simple, peu divertissant et, selon moi, particulièrement vide. Une caricature totale. Et surtout une caricature totalement surcotée...

texto: ¿Cómo alguien se pudo haber tomado en serio alguna vez esta película? Kubrick cree que ironía es burlarse y ridiculizar a gente que no puede defenderse (sus personajes). La palabra correcta es cobardía. La Tercera Guerra Mundial está por estallar y la única persona que parece obrar en forma sensata es el camarógrafo que dejó su cámara inmóvil y salió corriendo a protegerse. Los demás hablan hasta por los codos. Sólo se salva del naufragio Peter Sellers en su personaje de presidente (hace dos más). El resto del elenco —especialmente el pobre George C. Scott— es forzado por Kubrick a cometer indignidades seguramente prohibidas por la convención de Ginebra. Stanley Kubrick, eres un fraude. -Gustavo Noriega

texto: Eu fiz algumas pesquisas e descobri que Kubrick era fascinado pela guerra, não por glorificação militar e sim expor a fragilidade e irracionalidade humana. Em Dr. Strangelove Kubrick usou sua brilhante mente para juntar guerra e sexo em uma comédia. Durante o filme acompanhamos homens incompetentes tentando manejar uma guerra como se estivessem brincando num parquinho. Esse é um ponto que me fez rir, porque a crítica de Kubrick é extremamente real. Nas guerras atuais, ainda notamos os "fetiches" de homens no comando de potências globais se divertindo com o desespero alheio. A masculinidade tóxica pode nos levar (ou já está nos levando) a um futuro ridículo. E de novo, a cinematografia é incrível! O enquadramento dos personagens é crucial para uma interpretação mais perspicaz.

Les séquences autour de la guerre, notamment tout ce qui concerne l'avion et son crash, sont particulièrement bien faites pour l'époque, surtout quand on prend en compte le budget du film. Visuellement, ces passages sont beaucoup plus intéressants et montrent enfin quelque chose de réellement cinématographique. Les indications militaires, le contexte de la guerre et tout ce qui touche à la menace communiste sont également plutôt sympathiques. Ces passages sont malheureusement assez rares, mais lorsqu'ils arrivent, ils m'ont presque permis de ne pas décrocher complètement. C'est peut-être même ce qui m'a empêché de passer mon temps à faire défiler une émission politique comme si je pouvais simplement scroller pour passer à la prochaine émission. Bref, un huis clos ultra simple, peu divertissant et, selon moi, particulièrement vide. Une caricature totale. Et surtout une caricature totalement surcotée...

texto: “film and american society” watch #3 I cannot tell you how excited I was to finally watch this film, both due to its reputation and the admiration I have for Kubrick as a filmmaker, which is why is saddens me greatly to say I didn’t love Dr. Strangelove: or How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb . On one hand, I think it’s brilliantly written and effectively captures the simultaneously silly, absurd, and terrifying reality of nuclear warfare and the sociopolitical aspects fully in the hands of man. Naturally, it’s stretched to the extreme given its comically outrageous nature, but in many ways, Dr. Strangelove ’s sharp criticisms  remain relevant today: global annihilation, and consequently the fate of the entirety of humanity, is at the mercy of a bunch of horny, overzealous and incompetent men toying around with hydrogen bombs as if they were play things whilst comparing the sizes of their di-I mean missles. And given it’s a satire, I do find much of Dr. Strangelove to be humorous, and I did get a decent chuckle out of me from time to time. But at the end of the day, I really didn’t find this film to be all the funny. I just feel like it’s a tad bit outdated and, at times, too goofy for its own good. I can certainly see the appeal for others and Kubrick’s audience at the time of it’s release, but there were many instances  where I knew I should have been bursting out laughing, but at most was cracking a smirk. And as I’ve said in previous reviews, films focused solely on politics or historical events typically just don’t do it for me, and I think Dr. Strangelove unfortunately falls into that category for me. The acting is great (Peter Sellers in his triple performance and Sterling Hayden in particular are fantastic) and the story is well-written, but it was unsuccessful in fully sucking me into the chaos and panic of this world. I was sadly a bit bored at times (despite a rather short runtime) and was simultaneously hoping it’d keep going so I could get to a part I loved and wanting it to end. This film, in no way, shape, or form, takes away from my feelings towards Kubrick as an artist. As I’ve said before, I do think it’s cleverly written, well-executed, and impeccably shot film (might I add), with cinematography that once again proves he’s second to none when it comes to knowing the camera and where it should go. But the sociopolitical themes and darkly satirical humor of Dr. Strangelove just didn’t resonate or impact me the way I’d hoped they would. It pains me to say it, but this is my least favorite Kubrick as of now.

texto: I finally get why people call Kubrick a genius. I’ve watched plenty of political satires, but seeing Dr. Strangelove makes it obvious how much he paved the way for this genre. The movie isn't just funny; it's terrifying. He forces you to laugh at situations that should genuinely horrify you, laying bare how absurd and dangerous human paranoia gets when it's placed in the hands of powerful people. The most depressing part is how well it holds up. We haven't learned a single thing. Unhinged leaders are still taking the wheel, making you feel like it's a matter of when the bomb drops, not if. Strangely enough, that satire movie is right at my front door. At its core, the movie shows how much of this destruction is driven by fragile male egos and sexual insecurity. General Jack D. Ripper literally starts a nuclear war because he has erectile dysfunction and blames it on a communist plot against his "precious bodily fluids." Weapons become bizarre manhood symbols, and absolute destruction is preferred over looking weak or showing emotion. Even as the world is literally ending, the men immediately pivot to Dr. Strangelove's bunker plan because it guarantees them a harem of ten women each. It’s a brutal reminder that for men in power, war is often just an ego trip, no matter the cost.

texto: A film so contentious it needed a disclaimer at the beginning explaining how the events it depicts were in fact impossible, Stanley Kubrick's examination of Cold War paranoia is a black-as-night comedic satire with protracted, one-sided telephone conversations, the mighty George C. Scott performing one of the greatest unintended pratfall recoveries ever, production designer Ken Adam's fantastic War Room set (no fighting!), Slim Pickens riding the bomb, Peter Bull being unable to keep a straight face, Sterling Hayden going off the deep end thanks to fluoridation, and of course the legendary Peter Sellers showcasing his impeccable genius. An absurdist farce of the highest order. 4.5/5.

texto: Lifeless and dull. Stripped of all the intricacy and depth that made the original novel so captivating in the first place, the focus instead lies on making everything as big as possible, and the end result is a generic and overlong modern sci-fi blockbuster devoid of subtlety or warmth. Monotonous and self-serious, yet paper-thin in pathos. 2.5 hours of setup and exposition. In a movie already lacking a proper climax, the final act drags. Everything is loud and bombastic, but the characters themselves ring hollow; Chalamet lacks any charisma in the lead role. The film is more concerned with displaying its massive world than it is filling it with something to care for. The city of Arrakeen looks cold and barren– the opposite of lived in. Duncan Idaho is effectively relegated to two lines of dialogue: COME HERE & MY BOY. The dream visions of Zendaya's Chani come across like bad parody of 80s perfume commercials. All the charm and weirdness is removed in favor of a brutalist, drab aesthetic that seeps into all aspects of the film; gone is the magic and sense of wonder I found in the books. Happy it’s found success as I want more ambitious sci-fi adaptations, but this was a miserable experience and I’m starting to think Villeneuve might just not be a filmmaker for me.

texto: The biggest problem, though, is Hans Zimmer, whose score is incredibly loud and unremittingly the dominant sound for more of the movie’s 155 minutes than not. Zimmer’s approach to musical cultural appropriation has been blithe since at least 1994’s The Lion King , while his subsequent rise to Coachella fame has accelerated improbably. Both worlds collide in Dune ’s score, a nightmare barrage of field-filling drums punctuated by the odd muezzin-ish call to prayer—given how fraught the material already is (brown-skinned desert peoples vs. The Man), the Orientalist tinting is poorly thought through. Every time I went to the multiplex in summer 2016, I’d walk past an auditorium booming the thunderous punching-sounds foleys and Zimmer’s score from Batman v. Superman: Dawn of Justice , and it never failed to make my life a little more unpleasant. Five years later, the most cogent thought I emerged from Dune with was, “Hans Zimmer must be stopped .” More here .

texto: [...] Denis Villeneuve hatte also nur allzu Recht, als er sich dafür einsetzte, dass Dune nicht für das Streaming zu Hause geeignet sei. Das hat jedoch einen anderen Grund, als uns vermittelt wurde: Dune scheitert nämlich in epischen Maßen daran, ein vielschichtiges, gut erzähltes erstes Kapitel für ein unvergessliches filmisches Universum zu präsentieren, welches über die Grundgedanken der Romanvorlage hinausgeht. Das zweieinhalbstündige Science-Fiction-Epos kann weder für sich als alleinstehender Film überzeugen, noch als Exposition, so wie es gerne manche hätten. Vergleiche mit Stanley Kubrick sind ebensowenig angebracht wie mit dem ersten Teil der Der Herr der Ringe-Trilogie. Dune wäre zwar gerne so imposant wie letztere, wie ein moderner Lawrence von Arabien oder wie Das Imperium schlägt zurück, ist am Ende aber vor allem eines: Emotionslos, generisch inszeniert, holprig erzählt, inhaltlich unterwältigend, mit schablonenhaften Figuren gefüllt und in seiner gigantomanischen Machart ermüdemd - inklusive des brachialsten Zimmer-Soundtracks, den ich je gehört habe. texto: As grandiose as Dune : Part One presents itself to be, it does not suffice as a standalone film and as such, left me without catharsis and with the taste of something undefined on the tip of the tongue. Worldbuilding isn’t enough to tell a story, even with incredible visuals and set design and flawless performances from Timothée Chalamet, Oscar Isaac and Rebecca Ferguson — but this gave me hopes that the sequel(s) will give us cinema at it’s finest. Side note but I feel like I had such high expectations on Hans Zimmer and was let down with that orientalist ass score. It’s a bummer, considering that he declined doing the score of Tenet due to his commitment to Dune , but in the end didn’t come close to what Ludwig Göransson delivered.

texto: Excellent cinematography and direction…however, this has to be one of the slowest and dullest movies I’ve ever watched for a franchise of this size. It’s easy to see why this story was long considered unadaptable for the big screen. The film has the difficult task of introducing multiple families, political factions, key locations, religious themes, and complex world-building, all of which are challenging to translate from the novel to film. Denis deserves credit for making such a dense and difficult story coherent, but I don’t think the pacing works. I understand that much of the film is dedicated to laying the groundwork for the sequels, but watching it often felt more like homework than an engaging introduction to this world. I admire the craftsmanship far more than I enjoyed the experience. 3/5

texto: 他，回來了！Denis Villeneuve用熟悉的「慢條斯理」，來處理這份難以搞定的佳餚，手法幹練卻不失細膩之處，以一個沒看過小說的視角帶入，確實有難以消化的難處，但本片不至於像諾蘭那樣具有「干擾性」，而是可以輕易地貼近角色來了解架構的「引導」，然而，本片的弱點，也正是因受到原著及商業類型的束縛，導致成品流露出虛假與流於表面，最終成為另一部虎頭蛇尾的鉅作。題外話，如果你真要體驗到本片的壯觀，拜託去IMAX或ATMOS廳體驗，那種震撼與感動交織而成的「屏息」，難以形容。 《沙丘》算是維勒納夫中段班的作品，或許是因為有改編難度的壓力，整體看上來還是綁手綁腳的，不像《異星入境》與《銀翼殺手2049》那樣「放得開」，但他的導戲功力已達頂峰，大場面的調度讓人驚嘆連連，龐大的世界觀他也能處理得毫無匠氣、游刃有餘，從沙漠瀰漫的危險感，到室內空間的窒息感，都能捕捉到其深刻之處。劇情基本遊走在殖民與天選之子上，然而，劇本的空泛台詞與過度簡化，多少還是影響了兩個主題的力度，裡頭的傳承與戰勝恐懼的意象，則因為情節的不穩定，與兒戲般的轉折，讓這象徵意義變得薄弱，只剩「說出來」的表面意義。 說實話，如果沒了這群演員的表現，本片的角色塑造絕對會崩塌，裡頭我最愛Rebecca Ferguson的演出，她將眼淚化為角色的痛苦展現，母性的光輝清晰可見，隱忍與噴發的情緒拿捏得宜。漢斯季默，宛如為電影戴上一層淒美的面紗、穿上悲壯的戰衣，人聲總是能帶出電影最唯美的一面，可惜配樂的編排使整體情緒過滿，導致配樂干擾了劇情進行與情緒延展，人聲則因為頻繁的出現，給人煩躁的印象。聲音設計著實令人難忘，爆炸與打鬥的聲音富有層次感，衝擊力更是做得恰到好處，可惜，高亢配樂的過度氾濫，讓音效展現不了真正的實力。 《沙丘》在我看來，就是部相當適合大銀幕的作品，場面調度無懈可擊、音效特效傑出無比，創造出一場宛如《星際大戰》的視聽享受，可惜這場史詩，敗在劇情的單薄，支撐不了片長與大場面的輸出，《魔戒》之所以能支撐得了三個小時的打磨，就是因為劇本的可塑性及魅力，才能讓情緒持續延展下去，但《沙丘》犯了一個錯誤，就是用過多的篇幅來「介紹」，及彆扭的角色塑造，使電影少了收放自如的情緒，及大小場面切換的流利，更少了角色之間激盪的火花。 但這個缺點，仍無法改變本片是商業巨作的事實，Denis Villeneuve用極為藝術與富有情調的氛圍，讓影片既有沙漠的粗曠，也有人性的細緻，這，正是維勒納夫電影之所以吸引人的所在。然而，這只是《沙丘》的第一篇章而已，接下來，還有許多寶藏等著維勒納夫來挖掘，希望這告一段落的時間，能讓Villeneuve適應商業片的呈現。最後，一顆星給場景設計及特效的絕美，一顆星給眾星雲集的卡司，一顆星給Denis Villeneuve純熟的導戲功力。

texto: I really wanted to love Dune, but I didn't. Throughout the entire runtime I was waiting for one scene to hook me, to engage me in what's happening and allow me to immerse myself in the experience. But it never happened. For full transparency's sake, I read the book earlier this year and saw the Lynch film shortly after, so I went in knowing full well what the plot was and how another film adaptation handled the material. And while Lynch's Dune is riddled with problems in its pacing and plotting, there are things it suceeds in over Villeneuves latest endeavor. But we'll get there when we get there. The biggest problem in this newest adaptation of Herbert's seminal work is Villeneuves incessent gigantomania. When he said this film needs to be seen on a big screen, he was right, but I don't think any screen in the world will be able to make the size of this film look manageable. Every starship in this film is the biggest it can possibly be, Arrakeen, the capital of Arrakis, is an amalgamation of absolutely massive concrete buildings built almost on top of each other and the armies standing in formation seem endlessly big. Because everything is the enourmous size it is, none of it ever feels believable. When the courtyard of your palace is a massive concrete plain that stretches as far as the eye can see, but is entirely devoid of any markings, wells, walkways or any signs of life, they just look like computer-generated textures. When the ships are all huge grey blocks with no discernible characteristics or features, they just become big blocks that look artificially placed in an empty-looking environment. Dune is big because it is filled with literally huge structures and buildings and ships, but they never feel organic. Which is the next big issue. None of the sets the characters inhabit feel lived-in, or natural, or like they convey an actual world. Why Villeneuve opted for every building to be a grey slab with grey walls and nothing on them, I cannot for the life of me understand. None of its feels alive, vibrant, or remotely natural. It's all just copy-pasted textures that have nothing to them. Contrast this with Lynchs version and the lush round and gold features on the palace exterior and interiors, the beautiful ornaments and art-deco-looking elements. They have character to them, and they give a sense of personality to the area the characters are inhabiting. Villeneuves environments feel dead by comparison. Speaking of dead: To call the characters lifeless would be an overstatement, however, they do all have an air of imposed seriousness on drabness to them, that weighs down on the general atmosphere a lot. Never is there a sense of levity, of a character being content, and actually tender moments between characters are very sparse. The only actor that is allowed to have the slightest charisma is Jason Momoa, but even then he does not get the opportunity to let it shine much. Timothée is good at what he does, though he always looks like he's constipated. The rest of the cast has to abide by the general tone of the film, which is unflinchingly serious, to a fault. Again, Lynch was able to incorporate genuinely touvhing moments while condensing more story into less runtime, so why couldn't Villeneuve? All of these elements, the artifical scale, the lifeless set design, the one-note characters, it all leads to a very distant and cold experience. Never did I ever emotionally engage in anything onscreen, the film started and then it ended and I was left pretty unphased by everything. It's such a shame, because the book as well as Lynchs film both have spectacle and scale as well as emotion and very human moments. But Villeneuves Dune could have also taken place on an ice planet and it would have fit the tone of the film almost better. The main difference between the two films is that the newer really wants to take it's time and properly tell the story of Frank Herberts Dune. While Lynchs film tries to tell the entire story in two hours, essentially crippling it and leaving an overstuffed mess, the new Dune is intent on staying true to the details of what Herberts Dune is about. Except for the fact that there is still a lot missing. Not just details and single exchangeable scenes, but actual plot threads that fans liked (I know I'm not the only one upset over the plot line about the investigation into who the traitor is missing). So this new Dune is longer than the old one, and only tells half the story, but because the plot is decelerated so much the 150 mins feel like 240. The first hour of this film drags for very long, since exposition in reading is easier to digest than exposition in film, especially when in film it is just delivered through dialogue. At the same time, so much happens in this first movie already, that thinking about having to go see another one like this feels like a chore. It still feels overstuffed. Overall, this is definitely the better adaptation of the book Dune, though it is not finished yet. The second part is going to be far more interesting than the first, so I'm keeping my hopes up. In conclusion, while conceptually more mature and structured better than previous iterations, Villeneuves first Dune film can't help but bury its great base material under heaps of comically oversized imagery (Hans Zimmers oppressive and incredibly loud score only makes this film heavier and clunkier), an atmosphere that is way to stern and self-important for its own good and an approach to its base material that is taking its time, which has two sides, as it allows for more detail and clearer themes, but at the same time still seems like its barely managing to hit all the story beats before credits roll. This Dune needed more refining in a lot of places, and overall, its not bad. It's just not as good as everyone wanted it to be. I don't want to seem like I hated this film, so here are a list of things I liked: The cinematography largely supported the narrative quite well (though also succumbing to the aforementioned gigantomania) and generally looked pretty good. The CGI is entirely seemless (except for the artifical building exteriors and interiors). Everyone in the cast is sexy as fuck. The story of Dune is finally getting a worthy adaptation, though it is a flawed one. Might see this Dune again soon, might change my mind.

texto: I remember back in the days, after the first few Game of Thrones seasons came out, I thought that this show was quite bloated, filled with unnecessary filler and a story that would probably work better as a movie series à la The Lord of the Rings . Eventually tho, I started to realize that there might be more to it and when I finally read the books between seasons 6 and 7, my previous assumption did a complete 180. The show wasn’t bloated, it was rather a condensed version of an even more detailed book series, books that explained a lot of the things I didn’t get in the show, because there they were only mentioned briefly or left out entirely. I retroactively developed a completely new appreciation for the show .. until season 7 came around, but I digress. The point is, when Dune was announced, I immediately wondered, given my previous experience, whether it would be useful to read the books first this time, but I still didn’t end up doing it. The main arguments being: a) It’s written and directed by one of the most accomplished filmmakers of our time. He will make it work. b) A movie is supposed/designed to work on its own anyway. c) I simply didn’t want to spoil myself knowing the story beforehand, possibly robbing myself of some amazing cinema experience and d) I didn’t assume Dune could be anywhere as complex as Game of Thrones . Well, after having seen the film, I totally wished I had read the books, at least the first one. The movie has to establish a whole new sci-fi world with all its rules and features and Villeneuve does in fact invest quite some time to setup persons, cultures, beliefs, ideologies, items and a whole lot of other things that seem to carry a lot of weight for the characters, yet I still felt like I’m missing something to fully grasp why this world is how it is and why the people are how they are. As a result, I could never fully connect to the movie and therefore I didn’t really care all too much about anything or anyone. It was almost ironic that when I finally started to become invested into the story .. it was over. If Dune: Part 2 will get made, it might retroactively clarify a thing or two that didn’t reveal themselves to me in this movie alone, but the solution to all my problems might simply be to just read the books. I’m quite certain this movie will grow on me either way. For now tho, I’m just not really feeling it.

texto: Dune is great in every possible sense. The visuale are gorgeous, the sound incredible and the cast speaks for itself. But, at the end of its two and a half hours length, Dune had me praying it wasn't going to fade to black. Not without having even started its actual story. And just then it did, so I was a little upset. I don't think that this habit of making "part one" films is good. I rewatched LOTR The Two Towers a month ago or so, and it was beautiful. Without rewatching either the fellowship nor the return of the king (yes of course I know those by heart, but that's not the point!) Dune is not like that. It feels chopped, not complete; it can't stand up until something else will come out, and even then, it should only be watched as a prologue to that other thing. I don't think that's something I'd like to find in a movie. Nonetheless, I would suggest anyone to go and see, for it is a very nice experience.

texto: Peut être que le film était trop attendu ? Peut être que le défi était tout simplement impossible à relever avec brio ? Toujours est-il que je suis sorti déçu du cinéma ce soir. Denis Villeneuve, à qui l’on doit Premier Contact, film plein d’intelligence et d’idées visuelles fortes et originales, nous amène tout un plateau de préjugés hollywoodiens fades et redondants. Tout d’abord, l’histoire : Paul Atréides est l’Élu galactique qui veut sauver les peuples opprimés. Il comprend son rôle d’Élu en ayant des visions de l’avenir. L’histoire se passe sur une planète désertique, sur laquelle évolue un Vers de sable géant… autant de déjà vus. Soit, l’histoire n’est pas de Villeneuve, puisqu’il s’agit d’une adaptation de roman. Pour autant, la mise en scène n’a rien d’original non plus : là où la planète désertique aurait pu offrir de sublimes lumières, on se retrouve la moitié du temps plongé dans une demi pénombre d’où aucune lumière ne sait émerger avec grandeur. D’ailleurs, ce désert ressemble trait pour trait à celui de Star Wars Rogue One. En allant dans ce sens, les costumes ont l’air tout droit sortis d’une penderie de chez LucasFilm; et si un ou deux vaisseaux ont des design atypiques et plutôt réussis au début du film, on se retrouve vite à cours de bonnes idées. Les antagonistes - en bon méchants qu’ils sont - évoluent dans des décors sombres, ont des voix bien trop graves pour être réalistes, et respirent très fort. Une bonne idée survient tout de même à la fin du film : le bain noirâtre du Baron, qui intrigue tant par sa couleur que par sa texture. Bien qu’anecdotique, ce détail détonne tellement dans le champ visuel qu’il nous fait prendre conscience d’un défaut majeur du film : il manque de texture. Les décors en intérieurs sont tous beaucoup trop épurés pour être réalistes, et la peau des personnages (même ceux vivant dans le désert) est tellement lisse que ça en devient ridicule. En un mot : l’univers de Dune, tel que représente par Villeneuve, n’a pas de vie. Quelle déception également de voir Hans Zimmer au générique ! C’est donc lui qui nous a pondu des basses vrombissantes vues et revues pendant les scènes d’action, à la seule originalité d’une cornemuse trop discrète ? Ajoutez à cela un jeu pas toujours juste de Timothée Chalamet, et vous avez de quoi décevoir toute la population d’un salon de SF en un seul film… Pour autant, je ne me suis pas ennuyé durant les 2h30 (tout de même…) que dure ce périple galactique. Sans avoir été pris spécialement en haleine, j’ai été facilement et efficacement immergé dans l’univers Dune, dont on m’avait pourtant dit qu’il était complexe. En somme, c’est un bon divertissement hollywoodiens, comme tout un chacun a déjà du en voir une vingtaine. Quelques bonnes idées disparates, des plans assez jolis, un sound design très bien ficelé, et le tour est joué. Mais je pense qu’il faut être difficile avec ce film. Très attendu, il n’a fait qu’être un divertissement de plus qui permettra, dans 5 ans, de faire passer un dimanche pluvieux. C’est sans doute de là que provient la plus grande déception : on ne veut pas voir l’univers de Dune traité de la même manière aseptisée et stéréotypée que Star Wars, les Gardiens de la Galaxy, et toutes la ribambelle de licences qui s’en suit. Pour conclure, je ne sais pas si Denis Villeneuve a échoué à adapter Dune au cinéma. Il n’empêche qu’il a fait un film quelconque là où Franck Herbert, avec son roman, avait su modifier en profondeur la face de la SF.

texto: A  dark Sci-Fi Messias Story with Timothee Chalamet as center person sounds so promising. One hour into the film, it is still building up all the storylines, with a thin layer of spirituality and meaning in Paul’s Visions. Tension is created by slow and dark scenes, but the picture needs way too much sound to make things work (Hans Zimmer playing an all-in). The pacing is soooo slow, they might want to squeeze three movies out of the book. Great effects, great visuals, great sandworm, great actors. It’s a real blockbuster movie 🍿 . But honestly, such stories make me tired. It’s a man’s world. I really hope mankind will be doing better than weird noble families fighting each other in 8.000 years. Without a single ironic moment. Needless to say, the Dune Magic created by David Lynch is entirely missing. I say sorry to the Villeneuve / Dune and Sci-fi and Blockbuster fans with bad comments on my estimated low rating. I‘ve seen the film, I know the one by David Lynch, I talk about the Movie not about the book. Go see it and write your own review.

texto: Do you think the worms would be snuggly? They are very cute! The main theme for this is so heavenly. Gives me chills. I absolutely love it. I love Hans Zimmer. But I think recently he hasn’t been at his greatest. He’s made masterpieces of scores, like Interstellar and Inception. But Dunkirk just was bad , Top Gun: Maverick score didn’t feel special, F1 score also didn’t feel special at all. But the score for this, amazing. Masterpiece. Okay, the cinematography is good, but not great. The first 20 minutes I was thinking that the cinematography was amazing. But after that it just went from “this looks good” at certain scenes and that’s it. I mean it just all looks the same. It’s all orange. Dusty orange. They did really amazing shots with it though, don’t get me wrong. But the cinematography was a let down because so many people say “This has one of the best cinematography of all time!” Spider-Man: Brand New Day had better cinematography than this. It’s great. I really enjoyed it. It’s a bang average 4 star film. It’s an amazing set up for what’s coming next. But that’s an issue to be honest. My only two issues was the cinematography was kinda disappointing and this just feels like a set up film. Don’t get me wrong, I really enjoyed this, setup film or not. But I’m hardly ever a fan of those. Especially risky if you don’t know that you could make a sequel. Luckily, Denis did make that sequel and the third and final one is coming out in December. So I can breathe easily. Like I said, I was really enjoying it. But since it’s so long and the school year just started so I’m tried as hell. Literally right after the 2 hour mark I started like dozing off. Not because I was bored, far from that, but just really tired. I would wake up like 5 seconds after so I didn’t miss anything, only happened like 5 times. I have a love and hate relationship with long films. I love when they are usually a solo film, but something like this makes me nervous (with multiple other films.) Because I enjoyed it and will watch the second one and third one in theaters. But just really don’t want to watch the second one because it’s much longer. I have time before December so I’ll watch it eventually. But I doubt this month or next month. But I will! I want to write more but I’m just too damn tired.. I did it guys, I finally watched Dune!

texto: Denis Villeneuve has delivered a masterpiece. From the opening scenes, you're completely transported to the harsh, breathtaking world of Arrakis. The cinematography is next-level-those sweeping desert shots and massive sandworms left me speechless. Timothée Chalamet nails Paul Atreides' inner conflict with quiet intensity, while Rebecca Ferguson, Oscar Isaac, and Zendaya bring so much depth to their roles. The sound design and Hans Zimmer's thundering score hit you in the chest. It's a slow, deliberate build that respects the source material without rushing. Not everyone will love the pacing, but for book fans like me, this is pure cinematic joy.

texto: To any Sci Fi enjoyers, I think this movie is an amazing choice to start with. Denis Villeneuve really grounded the sci fi epic & aspect. Like, Instead of those overly complicated planets where it’s super green-spaced worlds, the technology really feels weathered, industrial and in general just really heavy. In the film, it really does a good job of portraying how Paul is not a traditional hero. This adaptation of the novel is just so good, I really love how Part One feels really incomplete since it ends off before the “true journey” begins. I would also love to touch on how Timothèe Chalamet does a really good on portraying how Paul is throughout the film, from manhood to leadership. Lastly, the soundtrack from this film is simply amazing, Hans Zimmer’s use of non traditional instruments, heavy percussion, and distorted human voices is simply incredible. For example the track “Paul’s Dream” starts off as a very fragile, ethereal whisper then violently builds up into a deafening wall of bass. One critic I can definitely say about the film is not pausing to talk about the terms that was used in the book to this adaptation.

texto: Forse l'unico grande problema di questo Dune è che esattamente ciò che ti aspettavi da un Dune di Villeneuve. Molto debitore a Lucas (troppo alcune volte), poche idee visive davvero rivoluzionarie (mari di sabbia a parte, straordinari). Tutto è come già lo immaginavi. Ma è un bel tutto, il cast è scelto bene (Chalamet ci mette almeno l'impegno giusto), gli effetti sono pazzeschi, la narrazione procede fluida nonostante la durata. Nota di merito a Rebecca Ferguson: finalmente un ruolo femminile, di madre del protagonista, che non è solo una bella statuina ma che davvero ha un ruolo fondamentale nel film, e lei lo interpreta benissimo. P.S.: per chiamarlo Dune - Part One speriamo che abbiano davvero la certezza di finire il dittico, anche nei confronti di un flop molto probabile.

texto: Encensé, le cinéma de Ruben Ostlund ne fait pas mouche à chaque fois. Ici dans « Snow Therapy », le point de départ est accrocheur (la réaction « égoïste » d’un père face à une avalanche met en danger son couple) mais ensuite l’analyse se perd en redite dans une succession de scènes sans grand intérêts. L’histoire avance petit à petit et un bon 1/4 d’heure aurait pu être coupé pour dynamiser l’ensemble. Passable et pas indispensable.

texto: Christ, this really feels like a debut feature, with absolutely no timely command of tone. It's fine when it actually lands the drama but most of Force Majeur is just a hideous time prison languishing in dead air. This film takes so long to say absolutely anything and what it has to say about gendered competition isn't very interesting. This is a film that thinks it's considerably more uncomfortable, funny, and smart than it actually is. I get that these silent interactions are supposed to be awkward!! but these characters are far too empty and vague to justify these so-called "textured tableaus." Ostlund's other films work precisely because they aren't paced, shot, or acted like this.

tema: Masculinidade frágil e egoísmo do protagonista
exemplo: Várias reviews deste grupo criticam o comportamento do protagonista, descrevendo-o como um homem que foge do perigo e depois nega o ocorrido, revelando uma masculinidade frágil e egocêntrica que a esposa e os filhos precisam tolerar.
texto: A single moment of crisis shatters the image of proactive, protective masculinity Tomas and his family have constructed around him. Force Majeure employs a clinical, alienating aesthetic of minimalist compositions that drain the Alpine resort of any warmth or coziness. The pristine white snow and hotel interiors are like a sterile laboratory. Every lingering frame feels hollow. And at the end of it all, after the denial, the gaslighting, the breakdown... Tomas, having experienced no real growth beyond earning the pity of his children, is offered a foggy 'rescue' scene that feels entirely staged. His wife Ebba allows him to play the proactive protector so he can reclaim the image of his so-called masculinity and their children can reclaim a sense of normalcy. This is his heroic moment, right? He's a 'man' again, right? Wrong. The film immediately undercuts this false redemption in the bus scene, where Ebba is once again the proactive one. She alone confronts the erratic driver who can't handle the controls of his own vehicle, and she alone gets him to open the doors so everyone can exit to safety, while Tomas sits passively. But, this time, he's willing to admit a fault to a member of his family instead of denying it to the point of breaking everything and everyone around him. Yes, he does smoke. Yes, he has lied. No, he's not picture perfect. Maybe there's some small amount of hope for him yet.

texto: Si l'instinct s'éduque, jusqu'à quel point la panique est-elle tolérée dans un cadre éthique d'accord de responsabilités ? La société dénature-t-elle le darwinisme social au profit d'un habitus d'héroïsme seulement loué, mais jamais enseigné ? Pourquoi l'instinct maternel et le rôle du protecteur sont assignés sexuellement et non nourris par les deux partis équitablement ? Un égoïsme altruiste existe-t-il dans la sphère de la morale ? Tant de questions posées par Ostlund restées sans réponse dans ce film en marge de ses travaux, héritier de ses films publicitaires sur le ski et pionnier dans ses satires sociales. Du bon (l'état de santé du couple montré dans les distances au miroir, la rave party sans musique) comme du moins bon (les sous-intrigues sans réel intérêt, Vivaldi qui nous est asséné sans discontinuer et sans plus vraiment de sens à la fin),  et le sujet des failles de la famille trop exploité par le cinéma scandinave doublé d'une proposition déceptive passé la première heure, me laissent face à une autre avalanche cette fois plus personnelle: me faut-il apprécier la beauté de ce phénomène (quitte à y retourner), ou fuir comme n'importe quelle personne sensée sauf un père de famille digne de ce nom .

texto: Après être déjà passé par The Square et Sans filtre, il n’y a pas trop de surprise de la part de Ruben Östlund dans le contenu de Snow Therapy. Il nous livre donc son dézingage de l’image parfaite de la famille modèle où une situation servira à en révéler la lâcheté, l’égoïsme et l’hypocrisie. Pourquoi pas mais l’exécution a du mal à me convaincre. Ça ne me semble jamais prêt à appuyer sur ce qui se veut drôle et ce qui se veut gênant. texto: i've been seeing a lot of people on this app saying the drama is a lesser version of force majeure, and i couldn't disagree more. that comparison is reductive and unwarranted, and the only similarities they have is the aspect of looking at your partner differently after learning something alarming about them, and sparking conversations about what you'd do in these situations. but these qualities can describe plenty of other movies too! they both have vastly different approaches, with equally latent characters, but i'll say for my money, the drama is more entertaining, for better or worse. force majeure takes the scenic route to get to the inevitable, and it's static, detached cinematography isn't helping either. though i heard it's worth avoiding, i am now curious about the american remake more than ever.

texto: Esto es el ejemplo perfecto de como no hacer un remake. Los primeros 20 minutos de película son perfectos, la mejor introducción para dar el origen al reinicio de la franquicia,  el problema es la hora y 10 minutos de película restante. Historia horrible, personajes horribles, diálogos horribles, no banco a nadie en esta película. Las referencias a las películas anteriores estan buenas pero lo hacen porque seguramente sabían lo mala que es esta película. Nosé, estoy muy decepcionado, me da bronca que películas mucho más viejas se ven incluso mejor que esta. En cuanto a Jason, está muy bien, definitivamente es el más hábil de toda la saga, aunque en diseño me sigue pareciendo mucho mejor el de Freddy Vs Jason. Creo que no tiene nada que no tenga las demás películas y no da nada nuevo tampoco, ni la hubiese visto.

texto: Eu gostaria de dar um 3,25/5 (que equivale a 6,5/10) mas como não há essa opção vamos de 3/5 (que equivale a 6/10). Esse filme tem a proposta de copilar todos os 3 primeiros filmes de Sexta-Feira 13 em 1 só. Essa proposta dificilmente teria qualidade, mas por outro lado, poderia ser divertida. Essa é a versão mais Brutal que existe do Jason: Corre, usa arco e flecha, salta, é "inteligente" (em certo momento ele até pegou as chaves dos veículos para que as pessoas não fugissem) sem contar a força absurda. De todas as versões do Jason que já foram feitas essa é a que eu mais torceria para jamais cruzasse meu caminho (tirando a do Jason X, um Jason cirborgue é sacanagem). Infelizmente, o jason e a ambientação do filme são as únicas coisas que tenho a elogiar, os personagens são todos descartaveis, sem graça e desmotivacionais. Ps: Jared Padalecki ( supernatural ) está nesse filme, por algum motivo acho legal ver ele nesse tipo de filme, apesar que prefiro a atuação dele em A casa de cera .

texto: I absolutely LOVE Darek Mears Jason. Easily the scariest and most menacing Jason across the entire franchise. Always wished he got a sequel. If there's one thing the 2000s slasher remakes generally excelled at it was making their villians genuinely menacing with awesome designs. The 20 minute long prologue was KICKASS. Honestly the best part of the whole thing. Clay and Jenna are actually really likeable lead characters. It's not one of the best horror remakes but it's a fairly enjoyable, lean 90 minutes by the numbers Friday The 13th experience with a dark and intense tone.

texto: Friday the 13th (2009) throws the first four films into a blender and gives them a glossy reboot makeover. It looks decent and delivers enough brutal kills, but the script is weak, the dialogue stinks, and it desperately lacks self-awareness. Derek Mears is no Kane Hodder, and this Jason runs, sets traps and operates underground tunnels like an angry survivalist. More human, less supernatural, and simply not my preferred Jason. Entertaining enough, but completely forgettable. A sharper picture cannot save a blunt machete.

texto: the pacing and introduction to the protagonist was well done in the intro, although I feel like it could have given us more content focused on Jason along with the setting of the movie rather than focusing on a cast of characters and a subplot that are both rarely mentioned afterwards. the whole gimmick of jared padalecki looking for his sister isn’t used enough for it to feel significant, and when it is, it’s executed in a way where it’s barely important to any other part of the plot. looking at this from the standpoint of it being a remaster of an older film series, i have to appreciate how they were willing to change the main character enough for it to feel remastered, yet not distasteful to the original. like how they leaned more towards Jason having the mental age of a child and dealing with his physical state of a grown body, along with making him more of a violent and sporadic killer. this movie barely builds any VERY MUCH NEEDED suspense, so most of the moments that are supposed to be tense end up falling flat and fail to keep you captivated. the cinematography and camerawork made it feel like I was watching something on the Disney XD channel. they tried too hard to make the handheld footage feel authentic that it ends up having the opposite effect. the shaky handheld camera effect feels forced and exaggerated, making it more distracting than immersive. this movie is REALLY bad at being funny, and had a very mid conclusion.

texto: Dieser Remake hat es wirklich in sich, es ist ein guter Slasher. Wenn jemand, der noch nie Freitag der 13. geschaut hat, wissen will, worum es in der Reihe geht, liefert dieser Film alles ab, was man wissen sollte: Pamela Voorhees ist dabei, der Sack und anschließend die Hockey Maske, notgeile Teenager, das Camp Crystal Lake und Jason Voorhees in all seiner Pracht. Am Ende des Tages, für uns, die die Reihe jedoch kennen, liefert der Film jedoch auch nur das, was wir schon kennen, nur in besserer Qualität, was ja nicht unbedingt schlimm ist. Ich habe extra gewartet, bis ich mir den Killer-Cut zu Gemüte führen konnte, da es immer einen faden Beigeschmack hat, zu wissen, dass man nicht den kompletten oder nur einen geschnittenen Film sieht. Ich hab jetzt keinen direkten Vergleich, wie viel brutaler er ist, anhand der Sprache (ich schaute auf Deutsch, die extrended Scenes sind auf Englisch) konnte ich ein paar erweiterte Szenen sehen, aber bei der Gewalt wurde ja kaum gesprochen, daher weiß ich es da nicht. Trotzdem ist der Film sehr brutal und hat ein paar wirklich gute Kills. Zudem mag ich es sehr, das aus Jason nun ein schlauer Killer geworden ist. Er hängt dich über dem Feuer auf, damit du andere anlockst oder lässt die Axt in dir Stecken, damit du noch schreien kannst. Was ich etwas komisch finde, aber das haben die anderen Filme auch, ist, das man Jason wie einen Hund rufen kann. Ich meine klar, er ist ja im Grunde ein Kind, aber manchmal ist das schon etwas albern. Seine Unterirdischen Tunnel sind zwar etwas seltsam, wer hat die auch gebaut, Jason bestimmt nicht (woher das Wissen?) und wenn es jemand anderes war, muss doch jemand davon wissen. Außerdem kann Jason sich auch wieder teleportieren, aber das ist ja auch nichts neues. Ein sehr gelungenes Remake, welches dem Geist der Reihe treu bleibt, aber in Sachen Qualität und Brutalität etwas anpasst. Kann man sich gut anschauen.

texto: Looking at the Rotten Tomatoes score and other reviews for this Friday The 13th remake, it seems like most people pretty much hated it. But I actually really enjoyed this movie and had a fun time with it. I like how this remake wasn't just a complete copy and paste story of the original movie. They swiftly establish the lore and cover Pamela Voorhees' story in the opening credits which I really appreciate because whilst Pamela is the OG killer, with this franchise, everybody wants to see Jason . Also, the birth of the iconic hockey mask is shown nicely here. One of the most memorable things about this remake is that it doesn't waste any time getting to the action and kills and it sustains this energy throughout the movie. The opening sequence is one of the best I've ever seen in a horror movie. Just that sequence alone would make for a great Friday The 13th short film. It's absolutely brutal and incredibly effective. The rest of the movie continues like this. The kills are so brutal and gloriously nasty, especially that opening sleeping bag kill. Derek Mears as Jason Voorhees is probably my favourite portrayal of Jason in the franchise. He's brutally terrifying, aggressive and monster-like throughout the movie. I also like how this Jason is smart and adaptable. His whole underground tunnel system is pretty clever and it explains how he's able to get around so quickly. I will admit that the writing is very cheesy and sometimes just straight up silly and it can be a bit distracting from the fun, darker tone but it doesn't really bother me too much. Also, I think a lot of people's biggest problem with this film is just how annoying and cliche the characters are. But I think that works for this movie and I mean, have the characters in this franchise ever really been that likeable? Overall, this Friday The 13th remake is a really underrated and incredibly brutal entry in this iconic franchise. With the cliche characters, silly dialogue, brutal kills, cool lake house location and Jason going into full monster mode, this movie fully embraces Jason's cult iconography. It's just a damn shame that this never got a sequel and nearly 20 years later, we still haven't gotten a new entry to this iconic franchise.

texto: Friday the 13th (2009) was my first experience with the franchise, and honestly, I had a great time with it. It doesn’t try to reinvent the slasher genre, but it knows exactly what it wants to be, and it delivers an entertaining ride from start to finish. Clay was easily my favorite character. Unlike many slasher protagonists, he isn’t just trying to survive—he’s determined to find his missing sister, and I loved how he never gave up on her. I also appreciated how protective he was of Jenna, which made him someone I genuinely rooted for. Trent was easily my least favorite character. His arrogance and attitude made him impossible to like, so his fate felt well deserved. I also liked that Jason wasn’t portrayed as a completely mindless killer. He follows a distorted logic shaped by his obsession with his mother. Whitney survives because she reminds him of her, which helps explain his actions—but it never excuses them. Understanding a villain’s motives is very different from justifying their crimes. The film doesn’t introduce anything particularly new to the slasher formula, but I honestly didn’t mind. I enjoyed it for what it was, and as my first Friday the 13th film, it definitely made me interested in the franchise. Sometimes a classic formula is all you need when it’s executed with confidence.

texto: Honestly a pretty good adaptation of Friday the 13th. It takes inspiration mainly from the first three films in the series and translates it into a more modern, easily digestible version of the original movies. Also, the teenagers are pretty good, even if a bit one-dimensional, which is arguably appropriate. Aesthetically not the exact same, but it still looks good and has a distinct identity of its own. The teens are fairly decent this time around. They aren't great characters or anything, still lack depth, but they are at least fun to watch for the most part. It certainly helps that Jared Padalecki is in this movie, as he is the most interesting character besides Jason himself. He is searching for his sister, who plays the role of Ginny from Part 2, confusing Jason as his dead mother. Because of this, he kidnaps her and keeps her in tunnels beneath the camp, a new addition to the remake. Speaking of, Jason is portrayed quite well. This time, he is HAULING through the whole movie. I enjoy when Jason walks casually towards his victims, but seeing him sprint full speed is pretty scary too. He starts with the baghead from Part 2 and eventually gets the hockey mask from Part 3, found in a random barn. He also has some pretty brutal and efficient kills. I do wish the climax ended with him fully going into the woodchipper, or at least had an axe in his head to create that iconic top-right chip on the mask. Overall, not bad! It's a different story and a different kind of Jason. Definitely not a replacement, but a good interpretation. With this viewing, my Friday the 13th marathon is complete, aside from Freddy vs. Jason, which I plan to watch when I marathon the Nightmare movies. So, that will be coming soon!

texto: Dieser Remake hat es wirklich in sich, es ist ein guter Slasher. Wenn jemand, der noch nie Freitag der 13. geschaut hat, wissen will, worum es in der Reihe geht, liefert dieser Film alles ab, was man wissen sollte: Pamela Voorhees ist dabei, der Sack und anschließend die Hockey Maske, notgeile Teenager, das Camp Crystal Lake und Jason Voorhees in all seiner Pracht. Am Ende des Tages, für uns, die die Reihe jedoch kennen, liefert der Film jedoch auch nur das, was wir schon kennen, nur in besserer Qualität, was ja nicht unbedingt schlimm ist. Ich habe extra gewartet, bis ich mir den Killer-Cut zu Gemüte führen konnte, da es immer einen faden Beigeschmack hat, zu wissen, dass man nicht den kompletten oder nur einen geschnittenen Film sieht. Ich hab jetzt keinen direkten Vergleich, wie viel brutaler er ist, anhand der Sprache (ich schaute auf Deutsch, die extrended Scenes sind auf Englisch) konnte ich ein paar erweiterte Szenen sehen, aber bei der Gewalt wurde ja kaum gesprochen, daher weiß ich es da nicht. Trotzdem ist der Film sehr brutal und hat ein paar wirklich gute Kills. Zudem mag ich es sehr, das aus Jason nun ein schlauer Killer geworden ist. Er hängt dich über dem Feuer auf, damit du andere anlockst oder lässt die Axt in dir Stecken, damit du noch schreien kannst. Was ich etwas komisch finde, aber das haben die anderen Filme auch, ist, das man Jason wie einen Hund rufen kann. Ich meine klar, er ist ja im Grunde ein Kind, aber manchmal ist das schon etwas albern. Seine Unterirdischen Tunnel sind zwar etwas seltsam, wer hat die auch gebaut, Jason bestimmt nicht (woher das Wissen?) und wenn es jemand anderes war, muss doch jemand davon wissen. Außerdem kann Jason sich auch wieder teleportieren, aber das ist ja auch nichts neues. Ein sehr gelungenes Remake, welches dem Geist der Reihe treu bleibt, aber in Sachen Qualität und Brutalität etwas anpasst. Kann man sich gut anschauen.

texto: Honestly a pretty good adaptation of Friday the 13th. It takes inspiration mainly from the first three films in the series and translates it into a more modern, easily digestible version of the original movies. Also, the teenagers are pretty good, even if a bit one-dimensional, which is arguably appropriate. Aesthetically not the exact same, but it still looks good and has a distinct identity of its own. The teens are fairly decent this time around. They aren't great characters or anything, still lack depth, but they are at least fun to watch for the most part. It certainly helps that Jared Padalecki is in this movie, as he is the most interesting character besides Jason himself. He is searching for his sister, who plays the role of Ginny from Part 2, confusing Jason as his dead mother. Because of this, he kidnaps her and keeps her in tunnels beneath the camp, a new addition to the remake. Speaking of, Jason is portrayed quite well. This time, he is HAULING through the whole movie. I enjoy when Jason walks casually towards his victims, but seeing him sprint full speed is pretty scary too. He starts with the baghead from Part 2 and eventually gets the hockey mask from Part 3, found in a random barn. He also has some pretty brutal and efficient kills. I do wish the climax ended with him fully going into the woodchipper, or at least had an axe in his head to create that iconic top-right chip on the mask. Overall, not bad! It's a different story and a different kind of Jason. Definitely not a replacement, but a good interpretation. With this viewing, my Friday the 13th marathon is complete, aside from Freddy vs. Jason, which I plan to watch when I marathon the Nightmare movies. So, that will be coming soon!

texto: Como de costume, novamente Joaquim Phoenix interpreta um personagem impotente, meio fracassado, carente de admiração e amor. Esses sentimentos podem ter diferentes destinos em cada um de nós, mas no caso de Cômodo, produziu ressentimos, inveja e agressividade. Uma agressividade destruidora, capaz de colocar em risco aquilo que Cômodo mais almeja: o poder. Mas o que é poder para Cômodo? Ser o Imperador do maior império já existente? Não; é ser amado de verdade.

texto: Varning lite spoilers. Såg om denna efter att ha sett colosseum påriktigt och vi hade lite feeling. Han har lite aura ibland men annars: dålig handling, för mycket fightscener och dåliga karaktärer. Var det verkligen nödvändigt att Maximus skulle ha ett kärleksrelation med Lucilla ? Hans fru hade precis dött och filmen hade varit lika bra utan att det fanns något mellan dem. Hela grejen att han saknade sin fru och barn med de små figurerna han hade med sig till slutet var ju jättefint? Men ändå skulle han ha en loveintrest?? Det enda bra var att han dog i slutet. Och jag har inte ens tagit upp att Lucillas son tydligen var hans trots att detta betydde att han varit otrogen mot sin fru. Jag vet inte. Hela den grejen kändes så sjukt onödig. Jag ville trycka igen på att det var för mycket fightscener. Visst, han är en gladiator och det kanske är behövligt, men ibland var det liksom 25 min av folk som slogs fram och tillbaka. Man blev lite trött när de inte ens var bra koreograferade.

texto: Gladiator is a great movie!! I just didn’t personally love it. The scale is massive, the set pieces are incredible, and Russell Crowe gives an iconic performance. Joaquin Phoenix also feels completely born to play that slimy, insecure Roman-emperor archetype. It really captures that classic old-Hollywood historical epic feeling. I can respect how good it is without feeling like it’s one of the greatest movies I’ve ever seen. Maybe the genre just isn’t totally my thing.

texto: A certain classic of a film, we see Russell Crowe's character embark on a plan of revenge and redemption against a backdrop of the beautiful ancient rome. An adopted son, the decorated general is chosen to succeed an ageing emperor with a dying wish to restore a roman republic, a vein son who couldn't accept the truth that he was not worthy. Commodus, played by Joaquin Pheonix, is the slimy and ultimately despicable antagonist. The whole film is beautiful and generally has some fantastic scenes.

texto: my name is Maximus Decimus Meridius esse nome dele é putaria!!!!!! genuinamente não tinha entendido o porque desse filme ter ganho o Oscar, até ver os concorrentes. Bom filme, divertido, as cenas de ação são bem feitas pra caralho. Tem um desenvolvimento foda, seja do Maximus, do Cômodo e alguns outros coadjuvantes. não achei que o russell crowe fez algo espetacular, mas de fato ele manda bem demais. Joaquin Phoenix é um psicopata de alto nível então o papel encaixou que nem uma luva e ele manda bem demais também e a Connie Nielsen merece respeito também pq dentre eles, possivelmente ela foi a que mandou melhor. no final das contas quem estragou esse filme mesmo foi o próprio ridley scott, o que ele faz de ruim nesse filme é de se admirar! Recortes paias e edições FEIAS PRA CARALHO pra um filme ganhador de oscar, o que tem um leve respiro é só a fotografia em alguns momentosos, figurinos (que nem é tão mérito dele assim) e a forma como ele consegue fazer os personagens morrer (destaque pra cena que a fdp é cortada no meio pela lâmina na roda da charrete parecendo um salame). dito isso, É ENTRETENIMENTO! A primeira cena no coliseu é uma PICA. Bom filme pra se assistir quando quer ver uma porradaria sincera com cenas de morte legítimas. E mesmo que esse bunda do ridley scott goste de distorcer fatos históricos e manipular a história do jeito que ele quer, nesse filme foi no mínimo honesta a abordagem política. ah e é meio datado também.

texto: A wonderfully ingenious and aesthetically appealing display of stop-motion animation — and, to me, little else. Guillermo del Toro ’s Pinocchio strikes me as a frustrating waste of technical prowess — namely, the visual presentation and impeccable animation work — with such tepid, handholding material beneath the charming carapace. While worthy and multifaceted topics are indeed tackled, they are done so with no novelty whatsoever (beyond the aesthetic) and mostly with the depth of an entirely unremarkable children’s story. The subject of death is handled somewhat better by the end, but at that stage the damage was all done. With a slew of obnoxiously obvious allegories and a cartoonish simulacrum of fascism, the film attempts to juggle far too much for its feebly thin central storyline to handle; and these characters are so numbingly banal and paper-thin, I couldn’t care enough to get invested in them. Pinocchio himself is an obnoxious embodiment of the ‘innocent outsider can’t comprehend evil’ trope, which is neither new nor interesting when this barebones, and his relationship with Geppetto is as uninspired and one-dimensional. The Cricket is a perplexingly unimportant piece of the puzzle, and when he’s not around it’s easy to forget he is even in the film — and as a narrator, he serves no purpose; most of the time, he simply explains the obvious. As a comic-relief, he is simply irritating. Performances are also mixed to say the least — David Bradley is probably the standout, but what he has to work with prevents him from excelling any further; beyond him, I am not remotely impressed. Ewan McGregor, Tilda Swinton, Christoph Waltz and Burn Gorman are all capable of truly exceptional work — but here they are all wasted; and why bother casting someone as skilled as Cate Blanchett in a role that anyone could have played? As for the central child performance, I’m not a fan either — no disrespect to Gregory Mann, who I hope has a long and prosperous career ahead of him, but I find him grating and offputting in the role, with most of his delivery being stilted and inorganic. Overall, an all-star cast squandered. I’m well aware of the unpopularity of this opinion, and it’s not like there’s nothing redemptive here — the animators are obviously master craftsmen who should be commended for their massive efforts, and I appreciate this adaptation taking risks and trying something new with the classic story (though it does amuse me that, even when set in fascist Italy and focussing on the inevitability of mortal expiration, this version is not even remotely close to being as fucked up as the original). I love the concept of Pinocchio having the embodiment of death as a mentor figure, but this — like the other interesting ideas — is never expanded upon in any meaningful way. Plus, the stakes are completely compromised, and goalposts are constantly moved; several frustrating deus-ex-machina moments — like the avatars constantly bending or breaking their own rules and impossible feats being brushed over — prevent me ever taking the characters’ plights seriously. To me, this is an assortment of potentially brilliant individual pieces that can’t form a satisfying whole, with the disparity between the surface-level whimsy and the profoundly unremarkable tedium of the actual content being wider than The Terrible Dogfish’s maw. I totally understand those who extol the former element, but I just don’t meaningfully resonate with anything else.

texto: A revisit and reappraisal of this film was not kind to it, for me. I rewatched most of Del Toro’s Pinocchio recently (can’t remember exact date so I’m estimating), mostly out of curiosity over how the film had gotten so much worse in my mind. In talking about it to a friend, I realized I didn’t like it anymore, whereas my initial viewing had left me mostly fond of it though equally baffled by it. Turns out, I don’t really like this movie. It always feels reductive to call a film boring, but I found myself uninterested in large segments of this film’s runtime. The animation is always impressive, in addition to being downright off-putting, and many of the character depictions and designs do a lot to magnify that off-putting sense. The messaging is painfully on-the-nose and heavy handed, even if it’s genuinely interesting here and there because, damn, it isn’t afraid to go to some dark places. And the songs? I hate the songs. I hate them so much. That Mussolini poop song? I’ll say I’m glad it exists, but that’s all, because how funny is it to say to somebody: “Oh, Guillermo Del Toro’s Pinocchio? Mussolini’s in it, and Pinocchio sings a song to him about poop.” There are still some scenes and moments of art design I truly love. And the final few minutes? Poetic perfection.

texto: I fear I have lost the childlike wonder that makes stop motion inherently astonishing to witness.  Please disregard if that inspires the disgust within you that it does within myself. That being the case, this only really kicks my butt visually when a particularly inspired design or specific sequence crops up (THRILLED at the wood sprite assembling of ghostly eyes which continue to blink around its wings e.g.).  One would hope that the musical numbers would provide this fairly regularly, but A: the direction isn't especially spry, and B: WOW the songs are so bad lmao.  I almost feel bad for how crassly I put that, but it was truly a jump scare every single time one started how bland and tuneless they were. Elsewise, this is left to its kid's movie bonafides and this just sort of happens to be a really annoying one.  Winningly grim in spots, willing to wrestle with things like alcohol dependency and fascism and death, but also every scene is so direct and repeatedly underlined.  For the kids, I don't blame it, but it's not gonna capture me in the process, to say the least.  Really it's a bad habit of GDT's in general (such a funny duology, this and Frankenstein), but his best movies have so much going on visually that offsets it.  Just happens to be one that runs kind of flat in that regard, too.

Love? horrifying! awful! nothing but pain and suffering? being a good person. same thing. Dude is the king of depressing dark fairy tales and that's exactly what this was. visually stunning, incredibly acting, soul crushing and depressing. If Del Toro learned anywhere near a single positive aspect of life, ever, his movies would be better. His masochism and misanthropy serve well in some films like Hellboy, but here it's just so wildly misplaced and heavy handed. Since getting accolades, Del Toro has gone from an incredible visionary director to an agent of pure sadness and depression. Great watch if you feel you want to throw yourself off of a cliff, after this film, you might.

texto: “Terrible, terrible joy.” Finn Wolfhard trying to be British… Ariana what are you doing here? First off, let me shower the visuals with praise. I adore stop motion and it’s such a good medium with which to tell a puppet’s story. The locations are beautiful and filled with personality, I love the designs of the characters so much. Inside the Whale looks especially impressively gross, but my favourite sequences of the whole movie are the ones in the afterlife with the Blue Fairy, who has a killer design. The hourglasses and the lighting and the hares bantering over cards all feel like they were engineered to appeal to me specifically. So so so cool. Also, using Pinocchio to explore father/son relationships and then how that intersects with the state, especially during Mussolini’s Italy is just such a creative concept and I love it. I do have a few complaints that hold this one back for me. I found it a little irritating until maybe Pinocchio’s first death scene - after that it kicked into gear and I liked it a bit more. It didn’t help that at first Pinocchio was an utter menace, causing more damage than The Cat in the Hat . Like obviously I do not agree with the fascists but they were right Pinocchio needs to lock the fuck in. A lot of the characters kind of grated on me, but they got better after that. The dialogue the whole way through felt a little clunky though. The themes are presented well enough on their own, you don’t need to explain them!!!! As much as I love musicals, I found the songs irritating because the scansion was off and they were all too short to really get a sense of their purpose. Don’t make a musical if you’re not going to fully commit to it!! Criminal that the best song in the movie is saved only for the end credits. Desplat still kills it with the orchestral stuff though, no surprises there. It’s no Pinocchio: A True Story , but it ain’t half bad. Also this would go crazy as a Next to Normal AU.

texto: Front-loaded film that teeters off as it goes on, but I did enjoy it overall. On a technical level, stop-motion animation doesn't get much better than this, but this film's visuals are held back by its art direction. Besides Geppetto, all the human character look lowkey scary, especially Candlewick and Count Volpe (whose design is just repulsive, and not in a good way). Everything else looked great though, including the titular puppet. I'm particularly fond of the "biblically accurate angel"-looking characters (who, much to my amazement, aren't voiced by Cate Blanchett, who instead, voices the fucking monkey). While we're on the topic of voice acting, it was surprisingly not great. No performance stands out as being especially good or especially bad; they're all just kinda okay. Also, the songs really did add NOTHING to this film. I could forgive their lack of relevance if they were actually good songs, but they're not (except for Ciao Papa, which was really sweet, and a major highlight during the latter half of this film). Nothing - I can't believe I'm about to say this - comes close to the quality of the Disney songs. *heaves* *wretches* *gags* Speaking of things that add nothing, I can't understand the Ewan McGregor glazing in these reviews. Bro did assolutamente niente the whole film. To wrap things up, we love ANTIFA Pinocchio, but the story surrounding him is too messy, tangential and episodic-feeling to feel cohesive to me. The emotional moments really didn't hit the way they should've, nor did all the themes this film tries to juggle, even if I could see the vision. I would probably revisit it though, and I'd definitely recommend it for the animation and the novelty of its story and setting.

texto: I definitely give this props for doing something new with the story (and I've never been a fan of it to begin with). The animation is great, but the songs really feel like an afterthought. I like the period setting that explores fascism, even though that also gets forgotten by the end. The father-son dynamic is certainly the best part, as that theme is carried from beginning to end (with both Pinocchio and Candlewick). The end itself, however, is rather anticlimactic.

texto: What Del Toro lacks in subtly, he more than makes up for in heart and beauty. The long-told, well-established story of Pinocchio gets completely flipped around and played with in this 2022 wonder of a watch. I loved how relationship between Gepetto and Pinocchio gets recontextualised with the existence of Carlo (the religious imagery in that one scene being outstanding) & also changing the setting to Fascist Italy?! Sure, that’s kinda fucking rad! If I do have a criticism, it’s that after the first song, the musical numbers just got less and less good (a fact clearly recognised by the filmmakers, as the songs became more and more infrequent to the point of nonexistence). And honestly, that one song did take me out of it a lil bit 😅 BUT, it would be entirely remiss of me not to mention all the things I loved about it too: 1. The stop motion animation art form always boosts the quality of a movie in my mind, they always have a little magic to them and this is no exception. 2. THE CHARACTER DESIGN?! OH MY LORD IT’S JUST FANATASTIC! So many times, I felt my jaw drop to the floor whenever a new character was introduced. 3. STACKED CAST (in a good way). 4. Grief really do hit different. 5. I had a really nice time watching it with Elz. 6. A wonderfully beautiful ending, that can be improved upon in no way, shape, or form. 7. I LOVE YOU EWAN MCGREGOR. And so forth. Fun ol’ watch, and AI could never make something so beautiful and expressive.

texto: I decided to watch this movie on a whim, just scrolling Netflix finding my next good watch, when this caught my eye. Of course I knew about it, I adore GDT and I heard nothing but good things, but I’ve never seen it. So I figured “why the hell not” I was then shot 57 times. I was not expecting this adaptation of this old ass story about a wooden boy coming to life to hit me so hard but I’m so glad it did. A beautiful story about grief and accepting that some things go, and you must move on. This film has some of the most gorgeous animation Ever put to film, a marvel of the technology and I shiver to think of how long this movie took. Excellent voice acting and shockingly good music that will remain in my head for a good long while, I have so much more to say about it, the time period, the themes, the use of history and war to set the backdrop. All excellent things, but that’s for you to discover! If you haven’t seen this movie, do yourself a favor and change that! Truly a marvel of film

tema: Falta de contexto político e covardia
exemplo: Algumas críticas apontam que o filme evita posicionamentos políticos e opta por uma abordagem asséptica, não explorando o conflito real.
texto: I am so very split on this movie. On the one hand, it brought me to tears, it is empathetic, it is beautifully shot. On the other, it is exploitative, ignorant, reductive. It presents one of the most violent, most disturbing, most saddening scenes and then undermines itself by needledropping a Radiohead song, playing it as safe as imaginable for a presumably western audience. Throughout the movie I was wondering, what country is this even about? I thought I missed an explanation and was trying to connect the dots, people speak Arabic, there is some kind of civil conflict in the 70s and 80s, there is a "Christian right" in conflict with a presumed (is it ever even made explicit?) left resistance. Why not make explicit that this is about the civil war in Lebanon? Clearly, the movie's relation to politics is as timid as Villeneuve's early attempts at making the landscape a character, conveying emotion purely through filming these very wide shots, but it always draws back before really going anywhere, seemingly afraid it would offend an audience's sensibilities. If the central hypothesis of Deleuze and Guattari needed any more confirmation, it is here that we find it: The main character's real life inspiration (Soha Bechara) was a communist soldier, the assassination attempt that landed her in prison was committed on a reactionary South Lebanese army general. But the movie stays fundamentally incurious about her motivations, about the motivations of the Lebanese armed forces, it has no interest understanding how people get so racist they commit these atrocities and it is especially afraid to be seen "taking a side". What the movie instead opts to do is write an oedipal drama; it is all about *family*. Politics, religion, personal convictions, historical situations, they all collapse into a backdrop to what really matters: Love, trauma, anger, all happening within the theatre of the oedipal triangle, mommy - daddy - me. I can't deny that said oedipal story did work on me and hit me emotionally, even more though I think it is a real shame how close this actually gets to being earnestly good and thoughtful. It wouldn't have needed much, all it would take is that this movie is less afraid of "politics", of "taking sides" and that it dares actually embrace a perspective on something instead of avoiding that by any means necessary.

texto: Jour 12 pour voir le top 100 Letterboxd Dans un pays imaginaire, après une guerre de religion, les enfant d'une mère ayant vécu ce fameux conflit tente de retrouver leur père et leur frère caché. Ce film aurait pu montrer les horreurs commises dans les deux camps, tout en mettant en évidence l'absurdité de ces conflits et de la haine qu'ils engendrent. MAIS… Il ne faut visiblement pas brusquer le monde du cinéma. Alors, plutôt que de mettre les deux camps sur un pied d'égalité, on va s'attaquer à ceux qui ne disent rien. Je vous laisse deviner ? ( NON ) Les Chrétiens. On a donc un film qui imagine un pays, qui suggère l'appartenance musulman de l'un des camps ( Clairement inspiré du Liban) mais qui, pour l'autre, n'hésite pas à multiplier les références chrétiennes : la Vierge Marie sur AK47 après avoir abatue de sangfroig un bus entier d'innocent, des croix montrées à plusieurs reprises, des discours chrétiens entre deux scènes de torture, etc. Alors oui, le film montre des atrocités commises par différents camp. Mais pourquoi insister autant sur l'iconographie chrétienne lorsqu'il s'agit de représenter la violence ? à force, cela mes un noms simple a retenir sur ces atrocité " Le christianisme ". Et c'est justement ce qui me dérange : si le but était de dénoncer les horreurs d'une guerre de religion, pourquoi ne pas donner la même place aux symboles et à l'identité religieuse des deux camps ? Pour votre gouverne, 4849 chrétiens ont été tués dans le monde en 2026, dont 93% en afrique, selon les chiffres d'Open Doors. Ce film aurait dû faire beaucoup plus de bruit. Edit : 4800 comme le nombre de personne qui on mis 2 etoile a ce film ;)

texto: ????????? The “gotchya” here being incestuous rape is so insane when the viewer would literally have NO WAY of putting it together because they used the same actor to depict a 15 year old and a 40 year old. There is no possible way the viewer can suspend their belief when the person we see commit the violence to The Woman Who Sings is LITERALLY A GROWN 36 YEAR OLD MAN. i just feel like i’ve had a really bad magic trick done in front of me that took 2 and a half hours of my life. I was actually really into this at first. I could feel some form of the twist burgeoning from the beginning of the second act, but actually just wtf???? It’s not even a “gotchya” it’s more of if they’d simply casted someone who even slightly resembled a young man or teenager I would have been able to make the connection without being explicitly told. The entire plots crumbles into nothing here. Look, the film was shot beautifully. Like I said i was invested, but In the end we have a lukewarm apolitical take that uses Arab lives as collateral for some “family is One” “Love thy neighbor as your brother” shit. Complete ignorance of the ACTUAL conflict that took place & is purposefully obtuse regarding the violence that was literally and TRUTHFULLY committed by Israel. I’m really really really not usually bothered by casting that may or may not be the “obvious” choice but the casting here literally obliterates this film. Nothing makes sense by the end of it. Hands down least favorite Villeneuve film I have seen. Still seated for Dune 3 but girrrrllll u pissed me clean tf off with this one.
