texto: Another one for psych class. This is one of the worst films I've ever seen. The performances are mediocre, with DiCaprio's likely being the worst. The writing is incredibly juvenile, even with the plausible theory that the majority of the dialogue is filtered through the guy's warped mind. The film doesn't even look good or have an interesting aesthetic. The twist falls apart because it requires you to empathize with DiCaprio's character in the beginning, which I did not. Now, to the big problems. This film's portrayal of the mentally ill is disgusting. I understand that the facility is specifically meant to house people who've committed a violent crime, but the film was arguably still irresponsible in its perpetuation of the stereotype that all people with mental illness are scary, violent, completely irrational, and are deserving of no empathy whatsoever. There is no mention of the specific diagnosis that any patient, let alone the main character, has, which makes it impossible to understand the accuracy of the portrayals. This film was made too recently to still exhibit such an under-researched and outdated parody of what a real group of underprivileged people is like. Let's move on to another problem, the film's portrayal of both the Holocaust and the implications of Project MKUltra during the Cold War. These were both serious tragedies that I feel were not handled with appropriate sensitivity and were rather just half-baked elements seemingly thrown in for added novelty. With this film exhibiting these two themes in addition to its portrayal of extreme psychosis, there are too many things being explored and none of them are done properly. The main conspiracy is clearly supposed to be MKUltra, something that really did victimize psychiatric patients during the Cold War, and yet in the movie's cannon, it's confirmed to not be happening. I don't think this film is intentionally trying to say that MKUltra didn't happen, but it's a very strange and poorly thought-out choice that is completely at odds with the setting. This movie clearly did not have anything to say about any of the incredibly serious topics it includes, and thus has no comprehensive or unique thesis. It's an offensive, confused mess that frankly has no merit as a piece of art.

texto: entretenida pelicula e interesante final, pero todo el aspecto “psicológico” de la pelicula lo senti muy cliche que me arruino el resto. muy fantástico para sentirlo real. sobretodo de personajes que deberian aterrizar los conceptos psicológicos. solo hacen que la pelicula se sienta mas como un “esto es lo que creemos que las condiciones psicológicas son en hollywood”. me saca de la inmersion y no pude evitar reirme. 5 estrellas si tuviera 14-16 años. muy dramatizado y caracterizado hasta sentirse holllywoodense, pero puede hacerse un espacio a la discusión teniendo en cuenta el cine noir, la pelicula no falla en hacer homenaje a los thrillers característicos de la epoca de estos, pero si senti que era muy “en tu cara”. no que no sea una peli entrete de ver. english: Entertaining movie with an interesting ending, but the entire “psychological” aspect of the film felt very cliché to me, and it ruined the rest. It was too fantastical to feel realistic, especially coming from characters who are supposed to ground these psychological concepts. They only make the movie feel more like “this is what we think psychological conditions are in Hollywood.” It took me out of the immersion, and I couldn’t help but laugh. 5 stars if I was 14-16 years old. Very dramatized and characterized to the point of feeling overly Hollywood-like, but it can still have a place for discussion when considering film noir. The movie does not fail to pay homage to the characteristic thrillers of that era, but I felt it was very “in your face.” not to say it was a fun movie to watch.

texto: "You have to let her go" "I can't!" "Then you'll never get off this island..." Enjoyed this more on rewatch, I was better able to appreciate how the mood of the island is developed, with the soundscape being particularly impressive, with original score, licensed music, and classical music all coming together really well. Weather is also used particularly effectively to make the island feel isolating and uncomfortable; there's something about heavy rain at night that makes me really uncomfortable and I love the way that is used in this film. The star segment here is Ward C, feeling like walking into a nightmare within an already dreadful environment - it feels like those segments in Silent Hill when you go from normal world to Otherworld, everything just gets so suddenly worse and terrifying with no end in sight. Despite this being a psychological thriller with heavy emphasis on its ending, it still does very little for me compared to the build up on the island (which I really enjoyed) and other films in the ending-heavy "genre" (Memento, Prestige, Fight Club, Total Recall, etc.). It just never feels like the reveals that happen meaningfully impact or re-contextualize the earlier scenes of the film. Of course the context does literally change but it doesn't really change the emotional impacts, at least for me

texto: Shutter Island is a psychological thriller film directed by Martin Scorsese and released in 2010. The movie stars Leonardo DiCaprio as Teddy Daniels, a U.S. Marshal who travels to a mysterious island with his partner, Chuck Aule, to investigate the disappearance of a patient from a psychiatric hospital. As Teddy investigates, strange events begin to happen, and he starts to question the hospital, the doctors, and even his own memories. The story becomes more mysterious and confusing as Teddy discovers that the island is hiding a dark secret. One of the best things about Shutter Island is its atmosphere. The dark setting, suspenseful music, and confusing events create a feeling of fear and mystery. Leonardo DiCaprio also gives a very strong performance as Teddy. The ending is one of the most surprising parts of the movie because it changes the way we understand the whole story. Overall, Shutter Island is an interesting and suspenseful movie that makes the audience think about reality, memory, and guilt. I would recommend it to people who enjoy psychological mystery films.

texto: I personally think it is a psychedelic paranoid masterpiece that is a wonderful examination of the brain, trauma, and crisis of identity. All themes which Scorsese has used before for his movies. The film is creepy, beautifully shot, extremely well acted, and leaves you in suspense until the end. While it may not break new ground the way Taxi Driver, Mean Streets, and Goodfellas do, it is one of the most beautifully shot films I’ve ever seen, and I find it quite emotionally impactful. So why do you think Shutter Island hasn’t aged as well as his other works? Even Scorsese himself said he regrets being attached to it, and I think that’s wrong because it shows just how versatile the guy is. He can direct any genre to perfection.

texto: First 50 minutes and the last 30 minutes are very enjoyable, but I found the middle of the film to be a bit clunky and all over the place. This is also where the movie loses its noir element and gets a bit silly. Leo is great as always and really stands out from the rest of the cast. I really liked Max von Sydow in his little role too. Scorsese’s use of music is great and very effective at building a hostile and unsettling atmosphere. I think the film not being in black and white was a missed opportunity, it would have fit the setting/vibe/score so well. I wasn’t too shocked at the twist tbh I thought it was pretty clear from quite early on. Shutter Island is enjoyable, but I don’t think it’s nearly as good as it’s made out to be….

texto: Oh, what a tangled web [they] weave…with this cacophony of story threads. The highly anticipated sequel to the Best Animated Feature Oscar-winning Into the Spider-verse opens this week, but unfortunately, it suffers from a bad case of sequelitis brought on by a gluttonous consumption of excess. Spider-man: Across the Spider-verse works in title only–and all too well, as it were. The title says it all, and that is precisely what audiences get in this comic philhar-tragic symphony in the key of overindulgence. Across the Spider-verse is what happens when a story idea doesn’t pass the elevator pitch litmus test (wherein an idea can be explained sufficiently enough in three-minutes or less). Quite simply, there is such a proliferation of story webs that there is virtually no plot–there is certainly no resolution before the (and this isn’t a spoiler) cliffhanger ending. Story webs lead into story webs that leads into even more story webs. Suffice it to say, it’s as if writers and producers took every incarnation of Spider-man comic series, threw them into a blender, and served the concoction o audiences. Unless you are read up on decades of Spider-man comics, you will be hard-pressed to follow any storyline. Perhaps the better expression of a collision of Spider-verses would have been in a television series that could have explores a different thread of comics each season. Clearly, Sony took the extremely positive reception of the first one, focussed on recurring praises, and amplified those to the nth degree. Never mind that more than the visual expression of the story, plotting is crucial to structure, pacing, and coherency. The animators and artists are showcasing brilliance in animated filmmaking, but the clear evidence of screenwriting is nowhere to be found. Without a well-defined central character, a well-defined external goal, and a well-defined character of opposition between the central character and the goal, there is no plot–merely a sequence of loosely connected scenes or fragments of ideas. A fever dream, if you will. While Across the Spider-verse suffers narratively, it certainly excels in the art of animation. The stylistic animation and editing is outstanding! Much like with the first movie, this one takes the emotive detail found in a single frame of a comic book (or graphic novel) and combines that approach with hand-drawn inspired motion picture animation. There are certainly problems with the story (or stories, as it were), but Sony Pictures Animation has demonstrably shown commitment to the boundless imagination of and capabilities of animation. Across the Spider-verse, in how it is expressed in this movie, can only happen within the world of animation. In no way could this movie be expressed in a live-action way. Perhaps the writers were asleep at the wheel, but the animators gave each universe of Spider-man characters its own color palate and animation style. Make sure to watch Across the Spider-verse in a premium format at your cinema, because the strength in this animated movie has little to do with the story as much as it does the stylistic animation. When a film, animated or live action, strikes a balance between style and substance, it can be enjoyed on the big or small screen without detracting from the storytelling; but when the movie struggles narratively but excels in form, then experiencing it on the big screen is the best approach.

texto: Man, I really wanted to like this movie more, I loved the first movie. And make no mistake, the first two thirds of this sequel were everything I'd hoped for, gorgeous animation and art style as expected, an interesting plot with a hilarious villain who unexpectedly goes through development into a more dangerous, malevolent foe. And the sheer amount of non-intrusive cameos when they arrive at Spider City, and Oscar Isaac's performance! But with the third act everything just... falls apart. All sense of momentum stops dead in its tracks. The bad guy fails to fulfill the menace and character growth he'd promised, because the movie never actually gets that far. What should be an exciting climax instead wastes time with useless drama and a misdirection that doesn't actually add anything to plot or character, but rather just bloats out the runtime to a level Eternals would have been proud of. And then.... "To Be Continued...... in Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse!" Uh.... okay. Sure. Cut out the third act of a film, the most important part of any movie where all the tension and drama pays off, and then relegate to a sequel which will likely not arrive for years to come. And instead of an alternate climax, just fill out the last 40 minutes with mind-numbingly boring and unsatisfactory screentime. Man, what a disappointment.

texto: I do not envy anyone given the task of following Into the Spider-Verse. That film singularly injected so much new life and artistic innovation into an IP that was beginning to get stagnant. It took the time and consideration to acknowledge the foundation and rich history baked into the character of Spider-Man and gave it a loving sendoff before turning to a brand new chapter. Regrettably, Across the Spider-Verse feels like one step forward, two steps back. If there’s one thing my journey through the MCU has taught me, it’s that the multiverse fucking sucks. And I understand that’s a contentious position to hold against a series called “the Spider-Verse,” but hear me out. Into the Spider-Verse used the concept in the most effective way: minimalistic. The multiverse purely acted as the inciting incident for Miles’ story, much like time travel in the first Terminator movie. Yes, you had cheeky references to established Spider-Man iterations, their tropes and standing in pop culture, but ultimately it was a measuring stick to hold up to Miles’ own hero’s journey. A narrative device showing how the character inspired this new hero, much like he has countless others in our own world. Comparatively, Across the Spider-Verse becomes overindulgent, languishing in its multiverse setting and using it as an excuse to showcase the less popular Spider-Man content, or ride the coattails of the more popular content. Remember Andrew Garfield Spider-Man? Look, there he is! And Toby McGuire! Look, this multiversal Spider-Man agency knows about what Dr. Strange was doing! And the dimension-hopping films? He talks to Mrs. Chen, from our hit Venom film series! The SPUM-C is alive and well. And look, there’s Donald Glover as Prowler! Like he was gonna be in the MCU! There’s also an attempt to make each dimension extremely unique, which unfortunately comes across like a more obnoxious attempt to copy the uniqueness of Into the Spider-Verse’s art style, and the clashing artstyles tend to make it look like a big, muddled mess. Really, with a concept like the multiverse, the last thing you want to do is get technical. Where Deadpool & Wolverine had the braindead concept of an anchor being, Across the Spider-Verse presents the “canon events.” (Which felt like such a dumb attempt at meta, I threw up in my mouth a little bit.) Rather than the shared trauma being a bonding point between the different iterations of Spider-Man, it’s now an absolute event necessary for their journey, whose disruption could lead to the disintegration of their reality. Delving more into the multiverse also takes the wind out of the sails for Miles’ own character arc. Spoilers: we find out that he wasn’t meant to become Spider-Man, as the spider that bit him came from another dimension. So he is an anomaly, and his arc is that, even though it wasn’t his destiny…he is still Spider-Man. Because he chooses to be. Which isn’t nothing , but feels like a much more hollow echo of his arc in the first film. My own cynicism and hangups notwithstanding, Across the Spider-Verse is a fine film. A far fall from its predecessor, but if you’ve been missing the characters and world, it does feel like a welcome return. It’s overbloated, and its standing as a definitive “part one” further lessens its value on its own, but it’s ultimately competent enough.

texto: my rewatch of this confirmed that this is the most tentative 10 i will probably ever have, because if beyond the spider-verse doesn’t pay off the myriad of things that were set up here, then this film will have aged so poorly. and this isn’t even just a “second movie in trilogy that hasn’t finished yet” problem either. dune 2 will always be a 10 for me no matter how horrible dune messiah is (although there is no universe where that film will be end up being bad). it is just so clear to me that this film exists to be a first half of a five hour film, and in ten years, when i inevitably rewatch this movie, i will be legally required to immediately watch the third one. and sure, you can go ahead and say that that’s the major flaw with this film. that it will never be a true story because nothing really concluded here. however, i don’t really care. this movie is just so fun to look at. every other scene had me asking how in the world this was made. and it’s not just all style either. there are moments in this film that do pay themselves off. gwen has a whole character arc here that has a fitting and emotional climax. miles does have a character arc here too that i would argue is paid off. he technically is finally ready to reveal the fact that he’s spider-man to his parents but he’s in the wrong dimension. anyway this is a 10 for me, and will probably stay that way if the third is also a 10. otherwise it’ll drop to like an 8 or something idk i’ll rewatch these in a year or two anyways so

texto: Я, лично, ничего тут не нашёл из «лучшей истории о Человеке-пауке», но она очень хорошая. Конечно, как гику такой фильм прикольно посмотреть, но явно не по мне. Да, тут много отсылок на пауков, много гик-намёков. По визуалу скажу: ЭТО САМЫЙ разнообразный СДВГ-контент вообще за всю Марвел. Первые 30 минут смотреть просто невозможно. ЭТОТ ФИЛЬМ ПРОСТО ОСТАНОВИТЬСЯ НЕ МОЖЕТ В ПОСТОЯННОЙ СМЕНЕ КАДРОВ И РИСОВКИ. Вырвиглазно порой было смотреть начало, но потом втягиваешься и фильм становится действительно хорошей личной историей Майлза Моралеса. Неплохо получается совмещать фильм-аттракцион, цветастое месиво для подростков, СДВГ-контент и неплохой сюжет о спасении и сохранении человечности. По сюжету в целом неплохо. Драматургия отличная и зашкаливает. Интересно, что всё таки фильм намного лучше развивает историю Мультивселенной, чем сами Marvel Studios. У Майлза, которому вообще 15 лет, начинаются самые тяжёлые годы в его жизни. Типичный подростковый период: с родителями плохо, друзей нет, в школе проблемы. После «Через Вселенных» у него ни осталось ни любимой девушки, ни друзей-пауков. Только обычная жизнь: родители, школа, несколько друзей и жизнь Человека-паука. Тем временем, у Гвен-паука тоже очень хорошая, даже местами чуть лучше, чем у Майлза, драматургическая сюжетная арка. Отлично раскрываются отношения Гвен Стейси и её отца, который искренне уверен, что Женщина-паук, которой является Гвен, убила местную версию Питера Паркера. В итоге, оказывается, что существует огромная мультвселенная, в которой вселенные пауков связаны Паутиной Вселенных. Мигель и его общество пауков очень хотят «защищать канон». И в момент жесточайшей битвы, она ссориться с отцом, который узнал её личность, и убегает вместе с другими версиями Человека-паука, в частности с Мигелем (чуть другой версией Человека-паука 2099). Интересно, кстати, сложилась химия отношений Майлза и Гвен. Им действительно веришь. Они выглядят, как хорошая пара-подростков. А ведь им действительно по 15 и 16-17 лет обоим. И когда наступает момент, очень больно они расстаются. Позже оказывается, что Мигель, пытаясь сохранять общие черты сюжета Пауков, хочет допустить смерть отца Майлза, который вот-вот стал капитаном. Типо якобы у Паука должны умирать всегда: Гвен Стейси, друг-капитан полиции и дядя Бэн. Ну, какой-то бред. В целом фильм хороший. Хоть и масштабно противоречит всем версиям Мультивселенной КВМ или «Человека-паука» 1994 года. Конечно, возможно, в этом и прикол, что Мигель врёт, удерживая собственное сообщество, как самопровозглашенную территорию, чтобы не пересекаться с Мадам-Паутиной из «Человека-паука» (1994) или УВИ из сериала «Локи» и типо это раскроется в третьей и финальной части. Например, чета никто не приходил в Киновселенную Марвел исправлять канон, лишь потому-что там не умирал дядя Бэн или не появлялась Гвен Стейси. Или никто не приходил во вселенную Тоби Магуайра, лишь потому-что его Гвен Стейси не умерла и её отец, капитан полиции, тоже не умер. Вот сюжетные противоречия, надеюсь в третьей части на этом они вывезут и всё свяжут отлично.

texto: Não sou tão chegado nesse quanto no primeiro. Não que ele peque no início; pelo contrário, é até empolgante ter as boas-vindas a esse universo novamente. O único incômodo que sinto é essa forma meio frenética da história, acelerada demais e com excesso de diálogos e comentários jogados com comédia excessiva. Mas acredito que, do meio para os finalmentes, é onde ele realmente compensa. Essa parte do Miles driblando mais de 100 cabeças de teia é coisa que a gente pede para ver sem nem saber: uma adaptação da genialidade do Aranha em combate. Trilha sonora, tensão crescente e diálogos com tom de mistério nesse desfecho praticamente fazem da melhor cena do filme.

texto: If Into the Spider-Verse felt like a comic book flipped at 24 frames per second, significant stretches of this one felt like it was flipped at 48. The animation is absolutely breathtaking, and the juggling act of all these characters, dimensions, and styles is remarkable, but the film’s constant need to stimulate becomes overstimulating: there’s always music, movement, and something happening in the background, rarely giving you room to breathe. The "Achilles' heel" of the multiverse concept is partly that there’s simply too much going on, and this movie occasionally falls into its own trap. The best parts are when it slows down. The Spot is introduced in an interesting way, but never really gets the one-on-one dynamic with Spider-Man you want from a central villain, partly because the emotional anchor is spread across so many characters that there’s nowhere obvious to attach yourself. It’s a double-edged sword: the concept is strong and the execution is often remarkable, but the emotional center is spread too thin. Still, the set pieces and animation are incredible, and the new dimensions it opens up are exciting. The ending leaves plenty on the table for the next chapter, and I’m excited to see where it goes. It’s still a very good animated film, but I prefer the first one, which somehow managed to balance all of this perfectly.

texto: my "remedial film school" project — catching up on the movies that most frequently turn up on greatest-of-all-time lists — has sometimes led to disappointments, but few have been as much of a struggle for me as this one. Admittedly it wasn't ideal viewing circumstances, pulling it up in fits and starts and consistently tuning out, such that it took me three or four sessions to make it through these two hours. I think it's just so unlike any film that I've seen before that I genuinely didn't know how to watch it, and the film was not in a hurry to teach me. Probably my biggest barrier is that it seems so disinterested in the humanity of everyone on screen — we don't follow hardly any characters consistently enough to get a sense of who they are as people, with the weird exception of Colonel Mathieu. Yes war dehumanizes everyone, but that doesn't mean the film needs to help the process along. Brahim Hadjadj plays Ali La Pointe as a sullen-faced silent type, which makes a certain amount of sense for his situation but makes him unengaging as the lead of a film. And the movie's weird dispassionate documentary-style tone means that I spent the whole time waiting for a moment of connection that never came. Time passes, people die, a series of events is shown, with little sense of causality or logic. But I suppose maybe frustrated restlessness is the desired effect after all?

texto: Not sure what all the fuss is about with this one. I give it credit for retelling actual events that went mostly untold and a nice large scale spectacle at the very end. Ultimately though this is a slog and entirely unremarkable, my partner even fell asleep. We follow the events of an attempted revolution headed by the Algerians against the occupying French forces. That's all that happens the entire runtime. Every single character that we follow has zero depth and all we know about them is they must kill the French imperialists or kill the people killing the French imperialists. There is almost zero weight given to the importance of this revolution, we don't really see how the French occupation negatively effects the Algerians, we do however see how the French was effected via the numerous terrorist attacks, but it's hard to sympathize with the French victims as they shouldn't be there to begin with. This isn't some deeply nuanced and enlightened approach to make us think critically about the cost of revolution, it's simply a shallow reshowing of events that don't deliver much emotional bearing. This movie spends all of its time on the failed revolution, and shoe horns in the successful revolution in the last 10 minutes. Battle of Algiers doesn't even hold up well from a film making perspective, as previously mentioned, the characters are surface level and the performances match. It's scenes of violence and "action" are very noticeably fake, removing all chance of viscera. This is a film that does not succeed on a story telling level other than to create a document of history, albeit even then only painting a minuscule fraction of the picture.

texto: While often enshrined as a cinematic masterpiece, The Battle of Algiers reveals itself upon closer inspection to be a technically flawed work of state-sponsored propaganda that priorities political utility over artistic integrity. It is profoundly shallow in character observation and attempts to substitute the hollowness of the narrative with the heaviness of the topic (colonialism). As this film was commissioned by the Algerian government and produced by an FLN commander, the impact of other Algerian resistance movements are completely ignored and instead the film is to function as a seemingly authentic origin story propaganda. The film’s celebrated documentary aesthetic is revolutionary, but is undercut by multiple weak formal aspects. The lighting in particular is jarringly inconsistent, often featuring blindingly bright front-lighting in scenes where no logical light source exists. Even between cuts of the same scene, the front-lighting persists into the new perspective, resulting in continuity errors and shifting shadows that shatter the very immersion the film claims to cultivate. This is compounded by an uneven sound design that lack consistency in dynamic and integration. Furthermore, mechanical cuts stitch scenes together without transition or narrative juxtaposition. As a result, the film feel like a collection of in-cohesive fragments that lacks vision. As mentioned previously, the film disguises narrative depth by the weight of its topic rather than by the quality of its writing. Despite the film's attempt to imitate observational realism, characters are treated as hollow ideological devices rather than real humans beings. The much applauded non-professional actor, Brahim Hadjadj, performs an Ali la Pointe that is painfully one-dimensional and mechanical, providing no window into the character's psyche (to the point that it is difficult to even recognise him as the protagonist). Ironically, the "villainous" Colonel Mathieu is given more complexity and range, feeling slightly more like a real individual instead of just a hollow political vessel. The film’s most egregious flaw is its poorly executed mechanical emotional manipulation from its sound and visual language. Death and suffering of Algerians are accompanied with religious scores and manufactured tears to evoke sanctity and martyrdom. In contrast, the death of European innocents are treated with cold, percussive score and lack of emotional outburst (even from themselves) to trivialise the tragedy. Disregarding the intent, the ostentatious and un-serious execution results in theatricality that ends up losing emotional grounding. Ultimately, The Battle of Algiers is less a work of art and more a technical manual for insurgency. It fails the "show, don't tell" rule with its paradoxical, dry narration and expositions that explains the how of the conflict while speaking little on the historical why. Concerningly, the film also directly proclaims the effectiveness of terrorism as a mean to gain UN support as well as the potency of torture (despite many research indicate otherwise). In the film's final scene, the irony of shouting for independence in the language of the coloniser is perhaps the film's most profound and most honest observation about the lasting scars of imperialism, yet unsurprisingly this is a depth that clearly escapes the interest of the film.

texto: La bataille d'Alger est un film incontournable sur la guerre d'Algérie, il est même le plus connu internationalement. Le film se déroule durant une période précise de la guerre que l'on appelle « la bataille d'Alger », période qui a duré de 1956 à 1957. Durant cette période, Alger devint un véritable champ de bataille où le FLN et l'armée française se sont livrés à des combats sans merci. Les deux camps ont fait preuve d'une extrême violence, notamment lors des attentats commis par le FLN contre des innocents ou encore à travers les tortures pratiquées par l'armée française. Cette violence, que l'on ressent tout au long du film, est caractéristique des régimes coloniaux, mais surtout des débuts de révolutions. En effet, Frantz Fanon , dans Les Damnés de la Terre , explique que la violence est une étape nécessaire pour que le colonisé, privé de toute initiative et de libertés intérieures et extérieures, retrouve ses droits. La violence extrême est donc nécessaire, mais elle constitue seulement la première étape de la révolution, elle n'est pas la révolution en soi. Cette étape de la révolte et de la lutte armée est la forme infantile de la révolution, c'est-à-dire qu'elle constitue le premier mouvement nécessaire, mais qu'ensuite tout le travail reste à faire. La révolte permet d'arriver à l'indépendance dans le cas de l'Algérie, qui devient officiellement indépendante le 5 juillet 1962. Ce mouvement d'insurrection fut impossible à canaliser pour l'armée française, malgré sa supériorité militaire, c'est pourquoi De Gaulle conclut progressivement qu'une Algérie française n'était pas durable. C'est donc par la violence et le courage que l'Algérie devint indépendante. Comme le souligne Fanon , le plus dur dans la révolution est l'après-révolte : une fois que les opprimés ont gagné, que faut-il faire ? Comment s'organiser ? En Algérie, Ben Bella fut le premier président en 1963, mais il fut renversé en 1965 par un coup d'État. C'est ensuite Boumédiène qui prit la relève en renforçant le poids de l'État dans l'économie. Des politiques d'industrialisation (Industries industrialisantes ou modèle Feldman-Mahalanobis) furent mises en œuvre, mais avec un succès limité, car cette stratégie d'industrialisation est autocentrée et nécessite donc une forte demande intérieure. Or, en Algérie, la population représentait alors moins de 40 millions d'habitants. Cependant, grâce au pétrole et au gaz (95 % des recettes d'exportation algériennes), l'État a pu financer certains projets tout en restant fermé au tourisme et à une grande partie du commerce extérieur. Aujourd'hui, les relations franco-algériennes sont tendues. L'affaire Boualem Sansal en est un exemple. Il existe toujours des frictions entre les deux États, notamment autour du Sahara occidental et du passé colonial français.

texto: I used to be funny and now I’m not so my very serious review is I hate the French and never want to go to Europe again. The FLN isn’t a tapeworm, Europe is. Nasty place full of nothing but hate. I wish this movie was more Algerian, or less Italian, or more the FLN propaganda film it was initially supposed to be. Why was this film more interested in occupation than liberation? This was just for other settlers to look at and be like look how much the French suck, we could never be that bad. Whole time we fucking are that bad. Whole time the Italians tried to colonize too, they just sucked at it. This movie kinda puts forth a progressive Israeli violence-on-both-sides type argument. But I still think it’s important for the profound effect it had, along with fanon, on the black panthers in Oakland. However I would never teach it while I would teach fanon despite his problematics. Watching this did make me think, what does it say that we give so much credence to fanon’s theories when the fucker went to Algeria speaking only French and never cared to learn tamazigh or even Arabic? Settler affinities, I guess.

texto: Film super cool sur la guerre en algérie, opposant le groupe de résistance contre le gouvernement français. Visuellement c’est très bien, les plans sont beaux, belle photographie, mise en scène excellente,  le jeu d’acteur époustouflant. A cela s’ajoute une écriture exceptionnelle, avec un rythme soutenu, et une reconstitution proche de la réalité des faits. Ça remets en question la place de la France en algérie à l’époque, ça questionne réellement le spectateur, puisque la réponse n’est jamais vraiment donné. La vérité montrée à l’écran suffit. Juste bravo.

texto: What impressed me most is that the movie refuses easy heroes. Both sides commit brutality. Both sides justify brutality. The French military often wins tactically. Raids, arrests, intelligence gathering, interrogations. The Algerian independence movement wins strategically. The film’s central point is devastatingly simple: An insurgency is not defeated when its fighters are defeated. It’s defeated when its cause loses legitimacy. The French win battles. Then lose Algeria. One of the rare war films that feels more interested in power and politics than victory.

texto: Un excellent film où le cinéma d’action moderne est né. Un film politique du réalisateur italien Gillo Pontecorvo. La manière dont le film est produit est juste glaçante, même radicale. Basé sur la lutte pour l’indépendance algérienne, c’est un film qui brûle la rétine et le cœur du spectateur, assistant à cela jusqu’au point d’éveiller les consciences. Les acteurs sont bien choisis et ciblés de manière très précise. On ne cherche pas de grandes stars hollywoodiennes mais des visages de haine marqués par cet épisode colonial, qui retransmettent leur identité de combattant au téléspectateur. Les décors également, on veut de l’authenticité jusqu’au bout. On tourne dans la vraie Casbah d’Alger où, quelques années auparavant, des guérillas avaient véritablement eu lieu. Les plans également sont aussi un chef-d’œuvre. La caméra, tenue par Marcello Mastroianni, jette toutes les règles et tous les codes du monde du cinéma, filmant à portée de main pour nous introduire dans le monde réel qu’a vécu l’Algérie durant cette conquête coloniale. Il filme comme on court dans la Casbah, comment on se cache, comment on respire ainsi que l’on combat. Des cadres parfois instables, flous, mais totalement choisis pour l’immersion la plus totale, avec un vrai style tremblant de réalité. En conclusion, un film d’une expérience hors norme, nous faisant vibrer tout au long du visionnage, en comprenant la vie des algériens durant 132 ans de conquête coloniale sanglante menée par la France.

texto: It’s a classic for a reason. There’s something so awe-inspiring about how visceral The Battle of Algiers comes across. From the gritty black and white, newsreel style filmmaking to the passion of the Algerian citizens, most of them reeling from  the real life events, all of them non-actors, there is a tangibility that only neorealism at its most effective can create. The plot mostly drags, I expected that, but there are so many things to admire. I especially loved that it didn’t shy away from the less pretty stuff and the gorgeous score from Ennio Morricone.

From picking people off the street to including the revolutionaries themselves, there is an air of respect — as Pontecorvo himself put it— to the "dictatorship of truth". texto: Auf dieses Nachbartreffen kann man getrost verzichten, denn: Anstrengend, aber im negativen wie nervigen Sinne. Kein Vorwurf an den Cast: Alle Vier merkt man die Spielfreude sichtlich an und ist neben der flotten Inszenierung stellenweise auch ansteckend, nur bleiben ihre Figuren zu uninteressant bzw im Falle von Joe und Angela (Wilde, Rogen) fragt man sich, warum die Ehe bisher so lange gehalten hat und andersrum, die biblische Geduld von Piña und Hawk (Cruz, Norton), denn jede:r hätte nach spätestens 15 Minuten bei der (passiv-)aggressiven Stimmung das Weite gesucht. Aber Olivia Wilde setzt weniger auf Glaubwürdigkeit, sondern mehr auf Übertriebenheit und das von Beginn an: Kaum ein Dialog oder Gestik kommt in dem mit unzähligen Sticheleien versehenen Schlagabtausch ohne Hysterie und Theatralik aus. Subilität hat Sendepause und mit Authenzität hat das auch nicht mehr viel zu tun. Sinnbildlich der Score, der die Gefühlslagen stets (über-)präsent sowie penetrant mit schiefen oder sanften Klangteppichen ausrollt. Später, wenn Wilde den Fokus hinter der (bröckelnden) Fassade blicken möchte, bleibt dieser auch verschüchtert. Wer A sagt, muss auch B sagen: Wilde bleibt bei A brav hängen. Allein nur explizit über sexuelle Vorlieben sprechen, ist halt lange nicht mutig genug, provokant erst recht nicht. Entsprechend gestaltet sich Eskalation ernüchternd inkonsequent, noch weniger entlarvend. Stattdessen werden dabei doch wieder die platten Gags rausgeholt. Das ist nicht pointiert, sondern peinlich. Die Komplexität der Konflikte um verschiedene Beziehungsformen und Liebe, aber auch Kommunikationsunfähigkeit, entfaltet sich dadurch selten schlagkräftig, auch da der Film lediglich auf konstruierte Zuspitzung aus ist. Am Ende stehen dann doch wieder Luxusprobleme im Vordergrund und die Tatsache, dass bei aller Offenheit andere Partnerschaftsmodelle außerhalb der traditionellen Ehe, doch nur pervertiert sind und Unruhe reinbringen. Ahja... Aber dann, die letzten 5 Minuten: Die sind plötzlich zutiefst menschlich. Olivia Wilde findet in der Ruhe nochmal leise Töne, die stark beeindrucken! Gerade hier ist zu spüren, was für ein reizvolles Potenzial 'The Invite' besitzt. Hätte sich der Film in den vorherigen 100 Minuten doch mal mehr aus der zahmen (Hollywood-)Komfortzone getraut.

texto: oh boy... this is without any doubt the worst movie i've seen in yeeears. and i'm not even a little surprised that it came out from some random woman named Olivia Wilde. we could see this movie as an image of Michel Foucault's worst nightmares. we all know that for a long time ago sex has been moved from its reality to "speech", speech about sex, and that we are making that mistake more easily today, but man, have you ever watched a movie where from the begining to the end every character thinks, speeks and fantasizes about sex, but there is not a single sex scene? penelope and norton are shown like "liberated" couple, they talk about their sex parties, orgies, swinger life and they are literally coming to dinner like neighbours from a floor "above". they think they behave like someone who has experienced freedom, but actually they are just playing by a different set of rules. they even have SEX MENU with "options" for their guests, its like bureaucratization of sex. man you are not free, you just serve a different power. you have to, if you want to be modern liberated person. so at some point in the film, they start acting like mentors, or teachers of sex life, while that other poor couple sees them like super cool and advanced lovers. because of those assumptions, they are forced to verbalise their sex life in front of the total strangers, hoping to find comfort and consolation. to make things even worse, the film suffers from a complete lack of measure, everything is overdone and shoved down your throat. there is way toooo much forced desire to be constantly comedic, on top of an already excessive obsession with sex. and speaking of painful overacting, Olivia Wilde is a disaster. she exaggerates every single reaction, turning every movement and expression into something completely unnatural and unwatchable. in the end, this movie is the ultimate trap, a piece of modern cultural propaganda disguised as progressive "liberation". as Foucault warned us, power doesn't just forbid - it also encourages us to speak, promising emancipation while tightening the leash. by selling us the lie that talking about orgies and using a "sex menu" equals freedom, this movie acts as a direct instrument of that power. it tricks us into believing we are breaking the rules, while we are actually just marching deeper into a surveillance state of our own desires. a total fraud from start to finish. also, who tf is Seth Rogen? is this guy a professional actor or what? he has only two states, one is when he is obviously angry, and the other one is when he is trying to hide anger. i feel sorry for anybody who calls him good actor

Wilde was outclassed from acting perspective (which isn’t saying much paired with 3 heavyweights) but I’m excited about her future as director. There seemed to be an odd general vibe of being a “commentary” but I don’t think it takes a complicated stance. Rogen and Wilde’s characters are miserable - but rogen’s character is evidently a more miserable and toxic partner. There might’ve been a “nobody’s perfect” insinuation but it was clear that Seth rogen’s character was far more imperfect than his wife’s. Usually with these type of relationship-character-driven single set dialogue movies you’ll see the narrative ask the viewer to fall on one side of a fence - but I don’t see what the fence was supposed to be here. This was a couple that probably should divorce. I didn’t see the complicated aspect since there was never a redeeming interaction between them in the brief 2 hours we shared with them. The sexually adventurous, risqué couple (that was more of a metaphor than anything, for what Rogen and Wilde wanted to be - “the grass is always greener”) didn’t shine a new light on the main characters to me. If anything they just told us more of what we already knew. I saw this with Zac and felt that I had to defend my disappointment because he quite liked it. And at its surface, it’s entertaining through its laughs and our wide eyed reactions to the sexual taboos. But on a deeper level I think Olivia Wilde wanted to reflect a sort of societal/romantic commentary. Perhaps on monogamy? On complacency? None of the commentary had an impact on me because it was rooted in a couple that no happy person would ever hope to relate to. At times I thought the movie would be an oddball, weird, shock factor sex comedy. It probably would have landed a better score if not for the “therapy” final act which had me constantly wondering why the second couple had not left an hour prior. I saw don’t worry darling twice and loved it but this one from Wilde tried to (maybe?)  encourage relationship perseverance but gave us no reason to root for them.

texto: oh boy... this is without any doubt the worst movie i've seen in yeeears. and i'm not even a little surprised that it came out from some random woman named Olivia Wilde. we could see this movie as an image of Michel Foucault's worst nightmares. we all know that for a long time ago sex has been moved from its reality to "speech", speech about sex, and that we are making that mistake more easily today, but man, have you ever watched a movie where from the begining to the end every character thinks, speeks and fantasizes about sex, but there is not a single sex scene? penelope and norton are shown like "liberated" couple, they talk about their sex parties, orgies, swinger life and they are literally coming to dinner like neighbours from a floor "above". they think they behave like someone who has experienced freedom, but actually they are just playing by a different set of rules. they even have SEX MENU with "options" for their guests, its like bureaucratization of sex. man you are not free, you just serve a different power. you have to, if you want to be modern liberated person. so at some point in the film, they start acting like mentors, or teachers of sex life, while that other poor couple sees them like super cool and advanced lovers. because of those assumptions, they are forced to verbalise their sex life in front of the total strangers, hoping to find comfort and consolation. to make things even worse, the film suffers from a complete lack of measure, everything is overdone and shoved down your throat. there is way toooo much forced desire to be constantly comedic, on top of an already excessive obsession with sex. and speaking of painful overacting, Olivia Wilde is a disaster. she exaggerates every single reaction, turning every movement and expression into something completely unnatural and unwatchable. in the end, this movie is the ultimate trap, a piece of modern cultural propaganda disguised as progressive "liberation". as Foucault warned us, power doesn't just forbid - it also encourages us to speak, promising emancipation while tightening the leash. by selling us the lie that talking about orgies and using a "sex menu" equals freedom, this movie acts as a direct instrument of that power. it tricks us into believing we are breaking the rules, while we are actually just marching deeper into a surveillance state of our own desires. a total fraud from start to finish. also, who tf is Seth Rogen? is this guy a professional actor or what? he has only two states, one is when he is obviously angry, and the other one is when he is trying to hide anger. i feel sorry for anybody who calls him good actor

texto: Auf dieses Nachbartreffen kann man getrost verzichten, denn: Anstrengend, aber im negativen wie nervigen Sinne. Kein Vorwurf an den Cast: Alle Vier merkt man die Spielfreude sichtlich an und ist neben der flotten Inszenierung stellenweise auch ansteckend, nur bleiben ihre Figuren zu uninteressant bzw im Falle von Joe und Angela (Wilde, Rogen) fragt man sich, warum die Ehe bisher so lange gehalten hat und andersrum, die biblische Geduld von Piña und Hawk (Cruz, Norton), denn jede:r hätte nach spätestens 15 Minuten bei der (passiv-)aggressiven Stimmung das Weite gesucht. Aber Olivia Wilde setzt weniger auf Glaubwürdigkeit, sondern mehr auf Übertriebenheit und das von Beginn an: Kaum ein Dialog oder Gestik kommt in dem mit unzähligen Sticheleien versehenen Schlagabtausch ohne Hysterie und Theatralik aus. Subilität hat Sendepause und mit Authenzität hat das auch nicht mehr viel zu tun. Sinnbildlich der Score, der die Gefühlslagen stets (über-)präsent sowie penetrant mit schiefen oder sanften Klangteppichen ausrollt. Später, wenn Wilde den Fokus hinter der (bröckelnden) Fassade blicken möchte, bleibt dieser auch verschüchtert. Wer A sagt, muss auch B sagen: Wilde bleibt bei A brav hängen. Allein nur explizit über sexuelle Vorlieben sprechen, ist halt lange nicht mutig genug, provokant erst recht nicht. Entsprechend gestaltet sich Eskalation ernüchternd inkonsequent, noch weniger entlarvend. Stattdessen werden dabei doch wieder die platten Gags rausgeholt. Das ist nicht pointiert, sondern peinlich. Die Komplexität der Konflikte um verschiedene Beziehungsformen und Liebe, aber auch Kommunikationsunfähigkeit, entfaltet sich dadurch selten schlagkräftig, auch da der Film lediglich auf konstruierte Zuspitzung aus ist. Am Ende stehen dann doch wieder Luxusprobleme im Vordergrund und die Tatsache, dass bei aller Offenheit andere Partnerschaftsmodelle außerhalb der traditionellen Ehe, doch nur pervertiert sind und Unruhe reinbringen. Ahja... Aber dann, die letzten 5 Minuten: Die sind plötzlich zutiefst menschlich. Olivia Wilde findet in der Ruhe nochmal leise Töne, die stark beeindrucken! Gerade hier ist zu spüren, was für ein reizvolles Potenzial 'The Invite' besitzt. Hätte sich der Film in den vorherigen 100 Minuten doch mal mehr aus der zahmen (Hollywood-)Komfortzone getraut.

texto: اكون صريح معاكم اللي اقل من 25 سنة مانصحه بالمشاهدة، لان الفيلم يحتاج نضج وتجربة كافيه عشان تستوعب موضوعيته، وهذا يتوافق  مع كون الفيلم مصنف R ومبني اساسًا حول زواج متعثر ورغبات وعلاقة زوجية طويلة، مو لان اللي بهالعمر مايفهمون،لكن كل ماكبرت وصرت تشوف العلاقات بشكل اقل مثالية، تبدأ تفهم ان الفتور داخل الزواج مو بالضرورة يعني ان الحب مات، وهذي اكثر نقطة حبيتها بالفيلم الفيلم ما يتعامل مع الفتور الجنسي بين الزوجين كأنه فيه شخص سيئ وشخص مظلوم، ولا يعطيك الحل السهل المعتاد، المشكلة انهم ما عاد ينجذبون لبعض بالعكس، يحاول يفصل لك الاسباب اللي ممكن تخلي شخصين كانوا في يوم من الايام مجانين ببعض يوصلون لمرحلة يصير بينهم هذا البعد، لان الزواج واقعيًا مو قائم على الرغبة طول الوقت، الرغبة تتأثر بالروتين، بالضغط، بالمسؤوليات، بالاستياء المتراكم، وب انك  تبدأ تشوف شريكك كجزء من حياتك اليومية بدل ما تشوفه كانسان مستقل تكتشفه كل مرة، وهنا الفيلم كان ذكي جدًا لان انجيلا وجو مو بالضرورة ما يحبون بعض، هم صاروا ما يعرفون شلون يحبون بعض بنفس الطريقة القديمة،وهذا فرق ضخم،  احيان العلاقة ما تموت، لكنها تتغير لدرجة ان الطرفين يفسرون التغيير على انه موت، وحبيت ان الفيلم ما كان خائف من الكلام عن الفتور الجنسي نفسه، لاننا ككبار بما فيه الكفاية نقدر نتقبل ان هذي من الاشياء  اللي ممكن تصير داخل الزواج، وان وجودها مو شيء فضيحة ولا دليل تلقائي على فشل العلاقة، الفيلم يستخدمها كباب يدخل منه الى سؤال اكبر،  هل الانسان يقدر يعيش داخل علاقة مستقرة من غير ما يفقد احساس  بأنه مرغوب؟ وهنا يدخل بينا وهوك اكثر شيء اشوف الناس ممكن يفهمونه غلط بالفيلم هو موضوع الـ open couple لان الفيلم مو قاعد يقول لك ببساطة شوفوا السكس الجماعي حلو جربوه، اشوف الموضوع اذكي من كذا بكثير، بينا وهوك موجودين كأنهم مرآة لجو وانجيلا، زوجين عندهم علاقة مختلفة تمامًا عن مفهوم الزواج التقليدي، ويبدون من الخارج اكثر تحرر واكثر راحة مع اجسادهم ورغباتهم، والاهم انهم يتكلمون عن الاشياء اللي الزوجين الاساسين صارو يخافون حتى يعترفون فيها لبعض، فالفيلم يحط نموذجين للعلاقة جنب بعض، واحد ملتزم بالـmonogamy لكنه صار مليان صمت واستياء وفتور، والثاني اكثر انفتاح جنسي، لكنه عنده مساحة اكبر للكلام والاعتراف بالرغبات والحدود، وهنا بالنسبة لي السؤال الحقيقي مو هل السكس الجماعي صح او غلط، السؤال هو هل المشكلة فعلًا في شكل العلاقة، او في الطريقة اللي الناس داخل العلاقة يتواصلون فيها؟ وهذي اذكى فكرة بالفيلم بالنسبة لي لان بينا وهوك ما كانوا مجرد الاغراء اللي يدخل ويخرب الزواج، هم كانوا catalyst، شيء يحرك العلاقة من مكانها ويجبر انجيلا وجو يطلعون الكلام اللي كانوا يدفنونه من سنين، حتى الغيرة، الفيلم ما يتعامل معها كشيء غايب بالعلاقة المفتوحة، تعامل معها كشيء لازم نفهمه ونتعامل معه، وعشان كذا هو مهتم بالتواصل والحدود اكثر من كونه مجرد احتفاء بالـpolyamory لكن بنفس الوقت، الفيلم ما يروح للنهاية اللي ممكن تتوقعها، وهنا اشوفه اكثر تعقيد، لان  الفيلم يفتح لك باب لقول ، يمكن الزواج الاحادي مو الشكل الوحيد للعلاقة، ثم بالنهاية يرجع يسألك طيب اذا فتحت كل الابواب هل فعلًا بتكون اسعد؟ وهذا اللي يخلي موضوع الـopen relationship بالنسبة لي اداة فلسفية اكثرمن كونه رسالة مباشرة بالنهاية الفيلم مو قاعد يطلب منك تتبنى طريقة هوك وبينا ولا يقول ان monogamy فاشلة، هو يقارن بين علاقتين عشان يكشف لك ان المشكلة احيان مو في القواعد اللي اخترناها، المشكلة في اننا نعيش داخل هالقواعد بدون ما نتكلم عن احتياجاتنا الحقيقية. برافو للمخرجة من اذكى رسائل الافلام اللي شفتها

exemplo: As reviews elogiam a direção de Olivia Wilde por sua habilidade em contar a história em um único cenário, com enquadramentos e uso de espelhos que enriquecem a narrativa.
texto: THE INVITE is an uproariously funny yet profoundly sad dramedy about a deteriorating couple who invite their sexually confident, free-spirited neighbors over for what’s meant to be a pleasant evening, only for it to spiral into something painfully awkward, ugly, and brutally honest. Seth Rogen showcases remarkable range, blending his signature comedy with the finest dramatic work of his career. Olivia Wilde delivers a soul-crushing performance fueled by anxiety and secondhand embarrassment, while her precise, assured direction turns this intimate chamber piece into an astounding seamless balancing act between humor and heartbreak with something meaningful to say about marriage and relationships. Edward Norton and Penélope Cruz are the cherry on top of what is a delicious offering from Wilde and easily the best directorial work of her career so far.

texto: I wouldn’t be surprised if The Invite finds its way into multiple Oscar conversations. I already complimented my favorite aspects in my first review, but man, everything was so well done here. Today’s audience really liked the humor and I think Seth Rogen in particular balanced everything so well, including the humor and facial expressions. Being able to pull off a combination of one of the funniest and most tense movies of the year is special. The way they filmed it — the artsy opening sequence (which also perfectly comes full circle with the ending), the camera/lens choices, the color grading, and the way they framed the characters and utilized foreground and background blur — was so good. The color coordination too. I love how the opening scene goes from them being happy at an undisclosed time to the beautiful frames of Joe just being miserable. This film is an excellent psychological study on self and marriage — communication, opening up, your perspective on the things you have, and resentment. Joe had so many good things going for him, between his daughter, kids learning from him, his musical talent, a pretty wife, and a nice home in San Francisco. He chose to be hung up on the past and push people away. Angela just had communication issues and made Joe feel unheard. You also see that the seemingly perfect couple indeed had their own issues, but Hawk was able to apologize when he was wrong and it was easier for him to be vulnerable. It also just shows how someone like him — someone you could easily judge or put into a box because of his sex life — had his own life experiences that you could empathize with. The end is beautiful because music can really break down barriers and be a language of its own.

texto: Very amusing, beautiful and touching, it spoke to me in a surprisingly introspective way - and stayed with me for a while. It’s a funny, stage play-like movie, focused on its quatuor - not trying to throw too much else at you. It’s contained is what it is. But it’s definitely more than just filmed theatre though. The framing uses mirrors, windows, character positions to express relationships. The colours are meaningful and the photography allows for contrasting warm glows and colder settings. The film’s grain also adds to this timeless and familiar look, totally adapted for a domestic context. And the film spoke to me, made me reflect on my relationship, which was the cherry on the cake. I’ll say the jokes felt sometimes too exaggerated for the grounded characters - like the wine scene. Certain twists were predictable. Also you won’t convince me that Olivia Wilde can be someone who’s uncomfortable about her appearance, but maybe that’s just me. The soufflé bit killed me.

texto: Every inch of this film was designed to make the audience feel smart for reading into the “fine print” that was actually neon signs. Every single one of the 1000 narrative payoffs was BEGGING to be recognized as a whisper instead of a shout, and I reckon most of the public did exactly so, given the rating. But it said it itself: “you don’t really want to work it out, you want to be fooled”. It’s so presumptuous, you could feel Nolan’s finger pointing at the threads he opened and hollering “LOOK LOOK THAT’S AN IMPORTANT DETAIL and then you can brag that you saw it coming”. Just essentially a kids movie. The cherry on the top of this big nothing cake is the theme of the film, what was it? Magic, obsession, supernatural? It switches up so fast I can’t seem to get a picture. They compete for their importance in the film and not a singular idea was developed, not a single idea won. No one won and the loser is the audience being tricked into thinking it’s smart by Nolan’s infantile attempt of directing what could have been a good film.

texto: After watching a bunch of nolan’s films consecutively, I have come to realise I really don’t gaf about the troubles of men who have left nothing but destruction in their path. The films always position themselves as a lesson that actions have consequences, but if the consequence is the loss of something so poorly written and badly fleshed out, the audience doesn’t actually understand the gravity of it. For example, if the lead’s wife dies, the assumption of his pain lies purely in our understanding of love and marriage. It does not depend on the actual film at all, and that’s where the films fall flat. Been trying to pinpoint what exactly makes the films so shallow and hollow, and now I finally do. All it took was being imprisoned on a plane which meant unwavering concentration to the content I was consuming. Oh also, I think I saw Dev Patel as an extra at some point.

texto: Wow this is such a weird film bc I went from mad abt the ending and honestly hating it to realise how much of a masterpiece this film is like it’s such a weird one. Big spoilers coming up x Ok the ending at first I thought it was kind of lazy, like I was waiting for something big but the fact they were twins was like the most obvious choice if u think abt. But then I realised that I didn’t rlly think abt it so like it’s a good ending bc I genuinely didn’t guess it bc it was in ur face the entire time. I thought it was rlly cool how that’s why he didn’t love Sarah all the time that was rlly cool. I loved how him being twins showed how much he would sacrifice for his magic, esp bc he lived the act like that was so edgy. I also thought it was rlly cool how Angier killed himself every night like that’s lowk dark but I loved it, and the ending scene with him in the water cage was quite cool. The obsession between the two men was quite fun to watch, but it got repetitive after a while, and I’m still not sure whether we’re supposed to root for one of them. I was on Angiers side at the start bc I still don’t get why Borden (still not sure which one) tied the knot like that I just don’t get it. I wish that was explained but I do think it keeps the mystery of it all, and I liked how sometimes Borden actually didn’t know which knot he tied, bc he was a twin. I loved the women in this film, Sarah was so complex and I hate Borden for what he did to her, all the lies and secrets were just wrong and I think it’s a big reason why I didn’t like Borden as a character. Genuinely the whole love thing was so sad, and when Freddy said he didn’t love her I was so shook. Her suicide was such a shock but it fit the tone of the film well. I also loved Olivia I honestly felt bad for her too bc I don’t think either man (Freddy and Angier) truly loved her like she was done dirty too. When she said they deserved each other it was such a gag tho icl. Overall, I was a bit bored throughout, and it was like the sixth sense when I was like waiting for the twist, but I didn’t rlly love the twist. I get it’s the point that it’s predictable and there’s so many clues which u ignore bc u ‘want to be fooled’ and I think conceptually that’s so cool, but I just hate the fact that initially I was just like ‘oh ok’ like it felt like the film was building up to mediocrity. Looking back and after my research I understand that the film is objectively a masterpiece, but it doesn’t rlly change my initial reaction.

texto: Nunca entendiste cuál era el fin. El publico sabe la verdad. El mundo es simple, miserable, es despiadadamente real. Pero si podías embaucarlos sólo un segundo, se hacian preguntas. Entonces conseguías ver algo especial. Esa mirada atónita en sus caras Me considero una persona muy interesada en la magia y a la cual le gusta ver trucos e intentar descifrarlos. Esta película más allá de usar ciencia ficción, también usa y revela trucos que se han llegado a hacer en la vida real y eso siento que enriquece mucho a la obra. Una vez más, se trata el tema de la obsesión y de querer ser el mejor o el más reconocido en un ámbito. Y, como ya es sabido, estos comportamientos no suelen acabar bien. En cuanto a la rivalidad entre los magos, me ha gustado mucho. Hay un motivo verdadero y de peso por el cual terminan así el uno con el otro. A partir de ahí, es un sinfín de manipulaciones el uno al otro, hasta que llega a su fin de un modo u otro. Centrándome un poco en la narrativa, a pesar de haber visto este recurso anteriormente de manera continua, siento que a esta película en concreto le viene muy bien. Hasta el último minuto de la película he tenido preguntas que se han resuelto en ese mismo momento y que me han dejado asombrado. En general he disfrutado bastante de esta película y estoy más que satisfecho. Aunque me hubiera gustado haber visto algún truco de cartas que conozco.

texto: 🍃Everything about this held up on a rewatch. I love how uncharacteristically (Nolan-wise) gritty this was. The London streets feel grimy and atmospheric while they host our main characters in an inescapable feedback loop of ambition and depravity. Bale’s performance is just unreal on a rewatch. The subtle physicality and expression work done to distinguish between the twins is crazy work. Jackman is also great, giving one of his best performances. The entire supporting ensemble is similarly excellent. The Root stuff stretches credibility for me and there is a moment halfway where the film feels slightly repetitive but I remained completely engrossed.

texto: The Good This was only my second watch, and I was impressed to find I liked it even more this time. The first time you watch The Prestige, Nolan pulls off a fantastic trick. He places the audience in essentially the same position as Angier. You become fascinated by Borden's secret because Angier is fascinated by it, and Nolan controls what you see and when you see it beautifully. And the reveal works so well, with the cost of obsession and sacrifice hitting all at once. The second time, the balance almost reverses. The ending may not hit the same, but the rest of the film works even better. You know the cost from the beginning, and suddenly every interaction is carrying something it couldn't quite carry the first time around. You’re watching Angier’s grief, bitterness and obsession knowing exactly where it's going to take him, and Hugh Jackman is fantastic here. There’s a desperation to him that develops so gradually that you can see him disappearing into it. But it's Borden who changed most for me on a second watch. Knowing his secret means you can see the cost of it written across virtually every interaction. Borden and Fallon, Borden and Sarah, the moments of apparent inconsistency, the distance, the things he can and can't remember, even the moments of genuine love followed by something that suddenly feels completely different. None of this was absent the first time. The reveal makes you understand it retrospectively. On a second watch, you get to live with it as it's happening. And there’s a wonderful symmetry between the two men. Borden gives up an entire life for the trick and can never let anybody know. Angier ultimately does something even more horrifying, all in pursuit of a version of the trick that, to the audience watching it, isn’t actually any better. That’s the beautiful punchline. He can finally be the man who appears at the back of the theatre and takes the applause himself. That’s it. Nobody in the crowd knows or cares what he had to do to achieve it. The difference only matters to Angier. Both men have sacrificed everything for something whose true cost can never be appreciated by the people applauding them. The Bad We’re scraping around here. One thing that bothered me slightly was Borden insisting that he doesn’t know which knot he tied when Julia died. Obviously, once you know the secret, there’s an explanation for why one Borden genuinely might not know. But surely the brothers talked about it? It’s such a monumental event in both their lives that the idea they could maintain uncertainty between themselves feels a little difficult to swallow. There’s perhaps an interesting reading where their identities have become so blurred that even responsibility is becoming shared between them, but I’m not entirely convinced the film earns that. There’s also some fairly aggressive plot convenience around Borden being convicted of Angier’s murder. He’s found at the scene, certainly, and Angier has constructed the situation to incriminate him, but everyone becomes awfully confident awfully quickly that Borden murdered him. In a film absolutely stuffed with doubles, deception, disappearing men and people whose entire profession involves making things appear to happen that didn’t, there isn’t a great deal of appetite for another explanation. It works because the plot needs it to work. And the meh... This was my second watch, and it leaves me wondering what happens on the third. The first time is a marvel, the second is richer. So what does a third watch give me? I had a similar thought after revisiting Inception. There’s always the possibility that once you've experienced the revelation and then experienced the film again with that knowledge, you've exhausted the major ways it can change beneath you. But my suspicion with The Prestige is that it will keep giving, because it's simply too rich beneath the mechanics of its trick. The secret isn't a replacement for the human story. It's the thing that reveals just how much of that human story Nolan had hidden in plain sight. And second time around, I could see it everywhere.

texto: A groundbreaking technical and atmospheric achievement that is so focused on imrpessing itself with what it can accomplish that it forgets how pointless it actually is until the very end, when it finally decides to cap things off with a grossly unearned, cliched, ham-fisted kindergarten-level moral conclusion. Ultimately not much more than pretty, bloated sadomasochistic survival porn, although it would have you think it's a spiritual, Terrence Malick-esque philosophical odyssey. It's not.

tema: Direção pretensiosa e excesso de estilo
exemplo: Críticas apontam que a direção tenta ser profunda e artística, mas resulta em exibicionismo vazio e falta de conexão emocional.
texto: There’s a sort of irony that, despite being a beyond exceptional technical directing talent who only gained the assistance of even more exceptional technical directing talent along the way, Iñárritu is by far the most graceless, hollow showboater Hollywood has seen in decades, arguably even more than someone as derided for showboating as Michael Bay. He’s a monkey’s paw curse made man: born with both divine technical ability and the worst possible thematic and narrative instincts those technical abilities could be paired with. Derivative, overly-literal macho faux-art nonsense. Historically irresponsible, burdened with clunky attempts at spiritualist visual metaphor and just way, waaaaaay too long. Lubezki can light and shoot snow-covered forests and babbling brooks all day but he can’t save a movie that, at its core, has nothing of any worth to say. Nothing truly relevant or engaging happens between those beautifully composed frames, save for a final shot that attempts to add deeper subtext the narrative itself does not attempt to possess. If you're after a “man fights nature/masculinity” movie set in a lot of snowy forest wildernesses that’s actually good, Joe Carnahan’s “The Grey” is a daring masterpiece.

tema: Direção pretensiosa e excesso de estilo
exemplo: Críticas apontam que a direção tenta ser profunda e artística, mas resulta em exibicionismo vazio e falta de conexão emocional.
texto: Could you imagine this in the hands of someone who should dig deeper into theme or actually put all this photographic marvel toward something interesting? What do we get from these extreme closeups? Michael Mann would know.  Or the dreamy spin of the camera? Mallick would use it correctly.  All these pretty pictures and a 1/2 way interesting story and the guy won’t even use a tripod or a track.  It’s obnoxious. In an attempt to seem “real”, the whole enterprise is lost because of the lack of connecting score that carries us through the scenes.  Movies aren’t just photography. This thing is inert, dead, and anything interesting we’re seeing or feeling is blunted by some show off camera nonsense.

texto: Un film qui avait énormément de potentiel sur le papier, avec une réalisation magnifique et des paysages absolument impressionnants. Visuellement, The Revenant est difficile à critiquer : la photographie est superbe, certaines scènes sont incroyablement immersives et la performance de Leonardo DiCaprio est clairement l’un des gros points forts du film. Mais malgré toutes ses qualités techniques, j’ai eu beaucoup de mal à vraiment accrocher à l’histoire. Le rythme est assez lent et j’ai trouvé que le film manquait parfois d’émotion et d’impact pour réellement me captiver. DiCaprio livre une performance impressionnante, mais même lui n’a pas réussi à complètement me faire entrer dans le film. J’ai surtout eu l’impression d’admirer la réalisation plutôt que de réellement vivre l’histoire avec les personnages. Un film très bien réalisé et impressionnant visuellement, mais qui ne m’a malheureusement pas autant marqué que je l’espérais.

texto: Leonardo DiCaprio gehört zweifelsohne zu den besten  US-amerikanischen Schauspielern der Gegenwart. Lange musste er trotz einer beeindruckenden Filmografie auf den längst verdienten Oscar als Bester Haupdarsteller warten. Umso trauriger, dass er mit diesem für  den Rachewestern "The Revenant" ausgezeichnet wurde. Von der großartigen Schauspielkunst DiCaprios ist hier hinter seinem Bart und unter dem Schnee leider wenig zu sehen. Seine Leinwandkollegen Tom Hardy oder die Grizzlybärin können diesen auch nicht übertreffen. Der von DiCaprio verkörperte Hugh Glass und der Pferdekadaver sind auch kein gutes Leinwandpaar. Dass DiCaprio sowie Regiesseur Alejandro González Iñárritu für diesen Film jeweils mit dem Oscar ausgezeichnet wurden, bestätigt noch einmal die Blut, Schweiß und Tränen-Ideologie der Academy.  Survival-Challenges oder dass man als Vegetarier rohe Bisonleber verspeist, scheinen wohl Merkmale guter Schauspielkunst zu sein. Es wirkt, als sei dieser Film vor allem gemacht worden, um bei der Oscarverleihung 2016 abzuräumen. Sieht man mal von den Schauspielern ab, hat der Film weder oberflächlich noch inhaltlich etwas zu bieten. Die Handlung ist banal und die Landschaftsaufnahmen erinnern eher an den Windows-Sperrbildschirm als an großes Western-Kino. Die Suche nach Spiritualität wirkt aufgesetzt, um der Handlung künstlich Tiefe zu verleihen. Es hätte ja ein interessanter Film sein können, der das Verhältnis von Mensch und Natur und die Themen und Fragen des Western-Genres aufgreift und neu verhandelt. Doche solche Fragen und Genre-Motive sind hier eher lose Assoziationen als bedeutungstragende Elemente des Films. Möglicherweise wird "The Revenant" nur dafür in Erinnerung bleiben, dass Leonardo DiCaprio für diesen Film seinen bisher einzigen Oscar als Bester Hauptdarsteller gewann.

texto: Infelizmente é muito forçado. Iñárritu está desesperado aqui, gritando para o telespectador que o que ele coloca em tela é MUITO FODA, ÉPICO, BRILHANTE, zero sutileza. Parece que depois de Birdman ele se perdeu na carreira. Filme pretensioso, mas que de certa forma é vazio. Se isso fosse luta livre, diríamos que é extremamente OVERBOOKADO, tirando a iluminação, nada parece natural, é tudo montado para gerar sofrimento, miséria e barreiras para o protagonista, para também canonizar como alguém bom e moral, esse é o principal motivo para a existência dos nativos no longa, aliás. Estilo e padrão estético elevado tem, claro. A fotografia é insana, o jeito que é filmado também. Gosto do jeito que lembra um videogame de sobrevivência em alguns momentos, é uma baita experiência e tem grandes cenas, sufocantes e tensas, como o do ataque da ursa, mas isso por si só não faz um bom filme. Eu nem digo que achei totalmente ruim, mas obra que está mais preocupada em se vender como arte do que realmente ser, não me pega muito.

texto: Ignorndo el complejo de salvador blanco que tiene esta película, resulta siendo una obra difícil de olvidar, sea por las bellísimas locaciones, la crudeza del guión, el oso cgi o la actuación de Leonardo DiCaprio que le hizo ganar su Oscar. La dirección de fotografía junto a las locaciones de la película hacen que estés las dos horas y media admirando el valor escénico de la película, que termina siendo lo más rescatable en mi opinión. Tom Hardy hizo un trabajo tan bueno que no supe que está en la película hasta que vi los créditos finales. The Revenant es una película evidentemente hecha para DiCaprio, todos escuchamos sobre el trabajo de preparación que hizo para el papel aprendiendo lenguas nativo-americanas, técnicas de supervivencia, etc, pero si esta información no se hubiera hecho pública, la actuación de DiCaprio habría terminado siendo otro casi-Oscar. Leonardo necesitaba un papel para un hombre blanco sensible y se lo dieron. La dirección de fotografía y storyboard carrean completamente a The Revenant.

texto: This has been on my watchlist since it came out and my friend braved the theaters with a box of chicken tenders she had to throw away because the violence made it inedible. I might have a different threshold for violence because despite the blood and gore, the only thing particularly shocking to me is that we are still making movies in which members of the indigenous population die so the white man can have motivation to carry him through each narrative beat. This movie is visually stunning. I love when the landscape becomes a character in and of itself and some of the cinematography is downright beautiful. I also loved the visceral camera work. You are zoomed unflatteringly close to faces or kicked aside in very smooth camerwork that anchors you in the action and splatters the camera lens. But I also had to suspend a lot of disbelief for this one. The human body can survive a lot, but . . . let's be real. He should have died like 10+ times. Infection, blood loss, blunt force trauma, hypothermia . . . Dude had a lot of ways out and somehow had enough energy to lug that soggy bear pelt around. (Also, how fast do hides cure?)

texto: The script is simple: revenge after injustice. The movie is built around the pain and suffering of Hugh Glass, who has his stepson killed by Fitzgerald after their settlement is attacked by Native Americans. A premise like that demands great performances to make an impact, and that's what holds the entire movie together. DiCaprio delivers it pretty well. It isn't one of his best performances, but it's a good one. Unpopular opinion: I believe Tom Hardy is the standout of the entire film! I don't usually expect much from him, and that's exactly why his performance is so impressive. Maybe the best character he has ever played. The whole time he is on screen, he grabs your attention. Simply as that. We've all seen dozens of revenge movies, but DiCaprio and, mainly, Hardy make this one stand out. The direction is great, and the scenes are raw, bloody, and aggressive. The soundtrack is subtle but works well. In short: the movie is simple, well-paced, and well-structured, and Hardy's performance makes it even cooler. OBS: DiCaprio has played several characters better than this one. It's kind of sad that "The Revenant" was the role that finally won him the award in 2016.

Ngl fair enough, bo gra postać niesamowicie wytrwałą i silną, więc szanuję. Co mnie boli najbardziej i co totalnie psuje mi jakąkolwiek szerszą wizję na ten film to wrażenie, że ta historia nie ma żadnego celu. Nie wiadomo co się dzieje, gdzie, kiedy i kto kim w ogóle jest. No i to co Glass był w stanie przeżyć strasznie triggeruje u mnie sceptycyzm i przekonanie, że irl to nie jest możliwe. Jedyne co mi się podoba tutaj to postacie. Motywy każdej są zrozumiałe na wiele odmiennych sposobów, co jest najzwyczajniej fajne, bo wzbrania przed obejmowaniem strony (z podobnego powodu podobał mi się serial Wikingowie). Powiedziałbym nawet, że żadna z postaci nie jest tutaj zła - po prostu ich sytuacja jest trudna. Najbardziej ciekawe jest to, kto z tej sytuacji wyjdzie najlepiej i odnoszę wrażenie, że jest to wszystko co film ma do zaoferowania. Poza tym, combo aktorów mnie zaskoczyło i w sumie to ładne kostiumy typy mieli. Nosiłbym.

texto: This has been on my watchlist since it came out and my friend braved the theaters with a box of chicken tenders she had to throw away because the violence made it inedible. I might have a different threshold for violence because despite the blood and gore, the only thing particularly shocking to me is that we are still making movies in which members of the indigenous population die so the white man can have motivation to carry him through each narrative beat. This movie is visually stunning. I love when the landscape becomes a character in and of itself and some of the cinematography is downright beautiful. I also loved the visceral camera work. You are zoomed unflatteringly close to faces or kicked aside in very smooth camerwork that anchors you in the action and splatters the camera lens. But I also had to suspend a lot of disbelief for this one. The human body can survive a lot, but . . . let's be real. He should have died like 10+ times. Infection, blood loss, blunt force trauma, hypothermia . . . Dude had a lot of ways out and somehow had enough energy to lug that soggy bear pelt around. (Also, how fast do hides cure?)

texto: The script is simple: revenge after injustice. The movie is built around the pain and suffering of Hugh Glass, who has his stepson killed by Fitzgerald after their settlement is attacked by Native Americans. A premise like that demands great performances to make an impact, and that's what holds the entire movie together. DiCaprio delivers it pretty well. It isn't one of his best performances, but it's a good one. Unpopular opinion: I believe Tom Hardy is the standout of the entire film! I don't usually expect much from him, and that's exactly why his performance is so impressive. Maybe the best character he has ever played. The whole time he is on screen, he grabs your attention. Simply as that. We've all seen dozens of revenge movies, but DiCaprio and, mainly, Hardy make this one stand out. The direction is great, and the scenes are raw, bloody, and aggressive. The soundtrack is subtle but works well. In short: the movie is simple, well-paced, and well-structured, and Hardy's performance makes it even cooler. OBS: DiCaprio has played several characters better than this one. It's kind of sad that "The Revenant" was the role that finally won him the award in 2016.
