texto: I did it! I watched The Revenant! What did I get out of the experience, you ask? First things first: Naughty Dog and Rockstar should be bending their knees to Iñárritu after ripping off their respective climactic fights from this film. The Revenant: probably in the upper echelon of "films I've never seen despite my age and preferences in actors and Oscar history." I remember watching the commercials before its release, but I was too young at the time to go see it (or at least too young to want to witness Leo crawl into the belly of a stallion). I have fond memories of the "Leo has never won an Oscar" memes, and endlessly watched WatchMojo's incessantness in crowning him in the number one spot for Oscarless movie stars. Despite my desire, the half-face Leo staring into the lens of the camera poster never caught my eye enough on streaming services to warrant a click (the 150-minute runtime doesn't help either, but this is also the guy who watched Oppenheimer 6 times, so take that claim with a grain of salt). Thank god HBO Max decided to blow the dust off of their Digger-related media this month. I've already watched Birdman, and I've started The Last Samurai (which doesn't look to be passing the Woke-ometer based on the first half hour). I'm taking the opportunity given to me and consuming myself with all the knowledge I can before the first of next month, when my most anticipated movie of the year comes out (It's Verity). A decade of buildup, the final episode when I finally watch the movie- does it live up to the hype I've built up in my mind... Um... Eh. Remember in The Last Jedi when they act like they're going to kill off Leia, and give her this really beautiful swan song scene, only to have her survive the attack and then never speak again throughout the rest of the trilogy. Like, yeah, that was all good and dandy, but what's the point? That's how I feel about The Revenant. Sure, Leo gives a great performance, the camera work is electric, and the cinematography is beautiful, but what does any of it amount to other than meeting those specified criteria? Why does The Revenant exist? Is it commenting on some greater cultural theme that 2015 audiences could resonate with? I don't see any. Is it trying to be an Odyssey-esque revenge story for Leo to shine in? I guess, but it doesn't do anything particularly unique besides replacing the Cyclops with a bear. I just see no reason for this movie to exist other than to watch people's eyes open in bewildered awe as you explain to them the basic plot points of the film. Happy for Leo, worried about Digger.

texto: "The Revenant" es la película modelo que deberían seguir todos los directores si quieren conseguir que su actor principal gane un Óscar. Para empezar, la trama es emocionantísima y deja momentos de una tensión brutal, como la pelea con el oso, en la que de verdad estás sufriendo mientras la ves. Además, a medida que avanza la historia, se va haciendo cada vez más evidente la diferencia entre los personajes que rodean al protagonista y el propio Hugh Glass, que acaba dejando escenas que quedan para la memoria. Más cosas que quiero reseñar de esta cinta son: • La actuación: Leonardo DiCaprio, dando vida a Hugh Glass, está brutal. Es una actuación de Óscar y está a un nivel estratosférico. Consigue transmitir muchísimo prácticamente sin necesidad de palabras y hace que sientas todo lo que está viviendo el personaje. El resto del elenco también está muy bien, aunque algunos aparecen durante tan poco tiempo en pantalla que no tienen suficiente margen para demostrar todo su potencial. • La dirección: Alejandro G. Iñárritu es un genio absoluto de la dirección. La manera en la que utiliza los planos consigue que el protagonista luzca todavía más y que cada momento tenga una fuerza visual enorme. La cámara está constantemente encima de los personajes y hace que vivas las situaciones prácticamente desde dentro, demostrando el enorme talento de Iñárritu detrás de las cámaras.

texto: Revisiting this almost ten years after I first reviewed it, and my impression hasn't budged: same admiration, same reservations, same grade. This is a film that demands something from you, and the rewatch was every bit as punishing as I remembered. Not a flaw, a design. The cold, the length, the sheer physical exhaustion of Glass dragging himself back to life all become something you endure rather than simply watch. On the technical side it is close to flawless. Iñárritu's direction is staggering, and Lubezki shooting on nothing but natural light gives you images you don't forget. DiCaprio throws his whole body into a nearly wordless role and finally got the Oscar he'd been chasing, with Tom Hardy just as good as the treacherous Fitzgerald. The lifelike makeup seals the immersion. Everything you can point a camera at, or build in front of one, is working at the highest level. Where it falls short is the script. The pacing sags in stretches, and too many scenes seem to exist for their visual force rather than any real narrative weight, beauty that doesn't always serve the whole. It's a monumental thing to behold and a hard one to sit through, and I respect it more than I love it. A survival epic that earns its greatness and makes you pay for every minute of it.

texto: I’ve been very scared of bears ever since I saw this in 2015. I had completely forgotten Tom Hardy was the bad guy. On rewatch the nearly 3 hour runtime felt long but worth it. I’ll take an artsy long shot of Hugh Glass staring up at a cliff and contemplating how he survived a fall that certainly would have shattered every bone in his body. You can feel the biting cold of the barren wilderness. The comforting cavity of a gutted horse. The final fight is as primal and ruthless as the American frontier. I ain’t afraid to die, I’ve done it already 🥶

texto: I forgot how truly amazing The Revenant really is; I truly believe it’s a masterpiece. Leo gives one of the best performances of his career as Hugh Glass; he barely has any dialogue throughout the entire film, but he doesn’t need it. The way he portrays anger, grief and (above all) pain just from facial expressions and motion truly captures the horror his character goes through. Tom Hardy’s performance is the complete opposite; visually he’s almost completely emotionless, but he builds his sneering, disgusting character through how he delivers his dialogue. The film is visually stunning; the way AJI and Emmanuel Lubezki contrast the natural beauty of the frontier with the harsh brutality of living and going to war in such an environment, truly captures frontier life in 1820’s America. The brutality sticks out in particular in The Revenant ; the bear attack scene looks so real that it’s actually difficult to watch - Rachel was nearly in tears. The makeup and prosthetics applied to Leo, combined with his performance, seems so so genuine, and the fight between Hugh and Fitzgerald at the end feels so real and human and not choreographed at all (like when he axes his fingers off!!!). Some people say it’s slowwww, or boringgggg or poorly written but they’re all incredibly wrong. It’s a harrowing, brutally realistic tale of survival and revenge and I think it’s perfect.

texto: Tudo que críticos (ou "críticos") ideólogos de direita dizem sobre Kléber Mendonça Filho, ignorando por completo as qualidades de seu cinema por causa do seu posicionamento político, eu vejo aqui: um filme não sutil e carente, carente de cinema. Vide seu panfletarismo realçado por um entorno muito pobre em termos de dramaturgia e linguagem (bastante televisivas). Sou voto vencido: é nesse filme de Anna Muylaert que eu vejo uma fanfic de esquerda sobreposta à arte cinematográfica.

texto: Filme médio pra ruim, do jeito que a cinefilia gosta. Recheado de clichês, não aborda nenhum dos temas com seriedade para ao menos alcançar alguma crítica social digna, como o filme parece tentar fazer. As personagens são estereótipos que se reconhece desde o primeiro contato: a empregada pobre coitada (e como de costume relaciona sempre uma pessoa da região nordeste como boba e ignorante), a filha iluminada que aprendeu sobre pensamento crítico (mas que no final das contas chama tudo de moderno e só sabe ser arrogante com o pretexto de uma rebeldia tosca e sem sentido), o filho maconheiro botão, o marido da patroa que é um herdeiro e abusador e a patroa super vilã. A proposta não é ruim, e é fato que o tema abordado é relevante, mas o filme se rende demais ao panfletarismo didático, que fica a todo tempo mostrando para o espectador o que ele deve achar e o subestima. No fim das contas, a filha da protagonista é a mais insuportável das personagens, os patrões não influenciam em quase nada senão por algumas expressões faciais, mas nada muito expressivo, e o final é simples, mas dá um fechamento que é linear com o filme todo, sem nada de muito surpreendente ou emocionante.

texto: “por que eu não posso entrar na piscina? eu também sou gente.” o filme não precisa de grandes falas para revelar as barreiras silenciosas entre patrões e empregados. elas aparecem nas pequenas coisas um olhar atravessado, um gesto automático, um espaço da casa que “não é para todos” como a piscina, a mesa principal ou o quarto destinado às visitas. quando a filha da val chega, essa ordem invisível se abala. a jéssica não se curva às normas que val aceitou por tantos anos, ela questiona e ocupa territórios que antes pareciam intocáveis. regina casé interpreta val com uma sutileza impressionante, misturando leveza, dor e um cansaço silencioso. ja camila márdila traz firmeza e ternura na medida certa, construindo uma personagem que desafia e inspira ao mesmo tempo. a direção de muylaert aposta em uma câmera que observa com frieza e distância, sem exageros ou sentimentalismo. essa escolha transforma momentos banais em cenas carregadas de sentido. o resultado é uma obra que fala de afeto, de desigualdade e da busca por lugar no mundo. é íntima e política ao mesmo tempo, mas sem cair na armadilha do discurso panfletário

texto: Uma sucinta review. Olá, apenas para os fantasmas do piso inferior. Sinceramente? É um filme e ponto final. Achei que seria um grande acontecimento, mas não vou performar falando a mesmice. Claro, posso dizer o meu dito óbvio, falar que é um filme que escancara uma desigualdade social que um sistema criou e parara pão duro e casca mole. Posso dizer que ver uma pessoa lutando para passar em uma faculdade é emocionante. Que o marido é um verme metido a artista e assediador. Que a patroa gosta de manter suas peças alinhadas no tabuleiro, jogando como bispo na diagonal, mas que claramente tem uma coroa em sua cabeça, podendo ir para todos os lados do tabuleiro. Que o garoto é um simples molecote padrão de uma família rica, já que para que irei pensar além da minha bolha se irei para a Austrália apesar de tudo? Que eu sou uma jovem que me acho superior perante a clara inferioridade que a sociedade me trata (e não, para quem se enxerga como superior, você não vai ser superior só por se achar superior). Que a Val é apenas alguém que está levando a vida, aceitando o que ela lhe dá, aprendendo a se rebelar contra pais (o capitalismo) que lhe diz não o tempo todo e a primeira palavra sussurrada de discórdia que sai de sua boca é uma grande vitória (entre na piscina, “roube” aquilo que era mais seu do que da pessoa que não se importava). Todavia, ainda assim a máquina vai girar, a luta vai continuar, ciclos vão estar ali a espreita. Como uma cobra comendo seu próprio corpo. Obviamente, as lutas farão a diferença, é plantando a semente do “você pode chegar lá” que talvez você realmente chegue. Até lá? Teremos outros lados das moedas para compreender, outros sentidos para desvelar,  não apenas interpretar de um modo tradicional por meio da dita lógica. Bom, digamos que decidi falar para talvez ninguém entender, mas saiba que em uma luta contra algo invisível, todos importam — independente de quanto você tem no bolso. Isso sendo em todas as lutas… temos muitas por sinal. Faça aliados, não mais inimigos. Digamos que seja o nosso Parasita. Digamos que não cause tanto espanto quanto, porém deve causar algo em quem gosta de ver o óbvio e se achar inteligente por saber interpretar ele. Até breve, Aly

texto: A pessoa já nasce sabendo, o que pode e o que não pode. Essa frase me marcou muito em Que Horas Ela Volta? , pois aqui é onde chegamos mais próximos do filme nos mostrar a raiz de todo o problema que a narrativa da obra nos sugere. Em outras palavras, por mais que saibamos que isso não é verdade, nos é imposto enquanto classe não dominante, desde que nascemos, que “naturalmente” temos um lugar definido na sociedade e que podemos até ascender, melhorar de vida, fazer “parte da família”, mas nunca estar no mesmo plano, mesmo lugar, mesma posição que a classe dominante, jamais. E é nesse contexto que trago o primeiro grande ponto positivo do filme: os enquadramentos. À Val, empregada da família, só lhe pertence um pequeno espaço, a cozinha, o quartinho pequeno e quente da empregada. Ela enxerga seus patrões através de uma parede que os divide, e portanto define muito bem o lugar de cada um. Ela só se junta a eles para servir e nada mais. No quarto dela, a câmera a filma atrás de uma grade, pois ela está presa e vulnerável dentro desse sistema. E o pior: por achar que é algo natural, que as coisas sempre foram assim, ela acaba acreditando que a vida dela é essa sem possibilidade de mudança. Ela cuida do filho dos patrões como se fosse seu, cuida da casa deles como se fosse sua, ela cuida de uma vida que não é dela e em troca deixa a própria vida e sua família de lado. Tudo isso por um valor financeiro baixo, injusto e explorado. É cruel. Mas aí entra o que seria o ponto-chave da virada: Jéssica, a filha de Val, vem para a cidade grande prestar vestibular e morar com a mãe (a quem mal consegue chamar de mãe, visto que Val teve que abdicar da própria família para ganhar a vida). Esse era para ser o grande motor de conscientização, mas, na minha visão, a personagem de Jéssica acaba sendo mal conduzida pelo roteiro. Não se trata apenas de uma rebeldia ou arrogância juvenil - o que seria compreensível, mas de uma falha no objetivo narrativo claro da personagem. Jéssica é pintada como extremamente inteligente, mas suas tentativas de conscientizar a mãe se resumem a gestos vazios, como dizer que ela pode entrar na piscina ou comer na mesa dos patrões, por exemplo. O que isso muda de fato no problema de classe? Na realidade material, se uma empregada doméstica decide usar a piscina dos patrões, ou ela sofre uma repreensão severa (afinal, eles detêm o poder financeiro e, por consequência, o poder sobre ela), ou é sumariamente demitida e substituída. Reduzir a emancipação de classe a esses "favores permitidos" esvazia a crítica. As falas e atitudes da Jéssica acabam soando rasas diante da grandiosidade do conflito que o próprio filme propõe. Obs: minha crítica quanto a isso é justamente a premissa narrativa política do filme, isso é esvaziado, raso, quase deixado de lado ao longo do filme. Ilustrando: A cena em que Bárbara, mãe da família, manda esvaziar a piscina depois que Jéssica entrou, falando que achou que tinha visto um rato ali é repugnante, é nojenta, dá raiva, mas isso no roteiro do filme não é explorado mais profundamente, não dá pra entender. Outra coisa que me incomodou: As cenas do pai da família com a Jéssica são muito constrangedoras também, até entendo o pensamento delas terem existido (hipocrisia e a objetificação velada da elite progressista…), mas mais uma vez cenas mal escritas e que no fim também ficaram sem sentido. O final também não me agrada, fica uma sensação de resolução simples que não resolve nada, afinal, se demitir do emprego explorador para finalmente viver mais de perto a sua própria vida junto de sua família, faz você de fato sair do sistema que anteriormente te fez abdicar de tudo isso? Não existe outra solução para ter uma vida mais digna junto das pessoas que você ama? Agora, o ponto alto do filme realmente é Val. Regina Casé brilhou aqui, personagem bem escrita demais, o filme é inteiramente dela. Fico de certa forma feliz de ter demorado um pouco pra ver esse filme, pois agora tive a oportunidade de assisti-lo com um olhar mais radicalizado politicamente. O capitalismo, como sempre a raiz do problema, dilacera famílias, criando um ciclo eterno de meninos e meninas perguntando “Que horas ela volta?” Um filme muito bom em expor o problema, mas pouco incisivo em mostrar a raiz, as soluções e uma conscientização mais crua dessa mesma questão. Ps: Adorei o fato de terem mostrado que o pai da família herdou tudo o que tem, ou seja, nos mostra que várias dessas famílias ricas e da elite herdaram seu patrimônio. Em outras palavras, essas pessoas não produzem nada, não trabalham, são vagabundas e vivem da exploração do trabalho alheio. 6,8/10

tema: Desigualdade social e crítica de classe
exemplo: As reviews deste grupo elogiam como o filme expõe a desigualdade brasileira e as barreiras invisíveis entre patrões e empregados, tratando o ambiente doméstico como um retrato das hierarquias sociais do país.
texto: Argumentos Desigualdade social. Distância socioeconômica entre as classes. Meritocracia: O esforço individual não é suficiente quando os indivíduos partem de condições sociais desiguais. Educação. Trabalho doméstico/direitos trabalhistas/ precarização do trabalho: naturalização da posição subalterna ocupada pela trabalhadora doméstica. hierarquização social: determinados espaços, comportamentos e privilégios sejam socialmente associados a determinadas classes/grupos. Mobilidade social.

tema: Desigualdade social e crítica de classe
exemplo: As reviews deste grupo elogiam como o filme expõe a desigualdade brasileira e as barreiras invisíveis entre patrões e empregados, tratando o ambiente doméstico como um retrato das hierarquias sociais do país.
texto: É uma verdadeira aula de dissecação social que expõe a crueldade sutil e enraizada do classismo brasileiro com uma precisão cirúrgica. Que Horas Ela Volta? vai além de apontar o preconceito explícito. O filme escrutina a violência velada do paternalismo brasileiro (onde "ser tratado como da família" é apenas uma máscara polida para a servidão moderna), transformando o espaço doméstico em um campo de batalha psicológico. Tirando um debate cultural de longa data dos seus trilhos narrativos mais comuns, a obra consegue lançar uma luz crua e implacável sobre as microagressões diárias e os ciclos de desigualdade que atravessam gerações. A direção de fotografia é surpreendentemente brilhante, com enquadramentos deliberados e potentes que mapeiam visualmente os distanciamentos emocionais e as fronteiras sociais dentro de uma mesma casa. As escolhas audiovisuais acertam ao conseguir transformar um ambiente doméstico e silencioso em uma arena de conflito visualmente marcante e instigante. A todo momento, a narrativa desfere golpes discretos, mas ainda assim amargos, àqueles que compartilham da consciência de classe. O que mais me pegou, no entanto, foi uma compreensão silenciosa: Ouvir o menino perguntar "Que horas ela volta?" no início parece apenas um aceno inteligente ao título. sinceramente todo mundo deveria ver.

texto: FILMAÇO DA PORRA! esse é um dos melhores filmes que já assisti em toda a minha vida. o filme aborda delicadamente a realidade de muitas empregadas domésticas no brasil. a val é uma personagem cativante porque eu vi a minha mãe nela. assim como a personagem, minha mãe também trabalhou em casas de famílias ricas e cuidou dos filhos dos patrões. na verdade, a val nem parece uma personagem fictícia, ela foi representada com tanto cuidado e naturalidade que parecia alguém que eu conheço há anos. e isso vem da atuação absurda da regina casé. a chegada da jéssica na casa dos patrões representa uma ruptura nesse ciclo de submissão vivido pela mãe dela. jéssica não aceita as imposições de inferioridade, e o filme deixa muito evidente o desconforto da elite diante da ascensão social das classes populares e do acesso às universidades públicas. é doloroso pensar que a val dedicou a vida cuidando do fabinho enquanto mal pôde acompanhar o crescimento da própria filha. o filme faz tudo isso de maneira extremamente natural e realista. as atuações são tão boas que eu sentia cada silêncio desconfortável e todo o resto na pele. e puta que pariu, eu ODIEI a Bárbara e aquele marido escroto dela. o fabinho talvez seja o “melhorzinho” daquela família justamente por ter sido criado pela val e por realmente amar ela, mas ainda assim continua sendo um playboy que parece incapaz de fazer qualquer coisa sozinho, igual aos pais que não sabem levantar a bunda da cadeira pra colocar um simples prato na pia.

texto: Assistir o filme da visão do “patrão” é algo diferente. A princípio, percebe se como a vida inteira da val foi servir a família e como ela é totalmente dependente dos patrões, tanto por morar na residência na qual trabalha, tanto pelo apego emocional no jorginho. Ademais, o filme mostra a filha da val como a quebra da herança de servidão. Apesar da plena ingratidão em seus momentos com Val e de momentos invasivos para/ com a família, ela foi fundamental para libertar sua mãe, que posteriormente a libertou da herança de abandono, possibilitando a vinda de seu neto a são paulo. Um filme incrível e forte, que mostra como a relação patrão e funcionário deve ser reformulada no Brasil, e como a desigualdade afeta e molda road as gerações inseridas nesse contexto.

texto: É uma verdadeira aula de dissecação social que expõe a crueldade sutil e enraizada do classismo brasileiro com uma precisão cirúrgica. Que Horas Ela Volta? vai além de apontar o preconceito explícito. O filme escrutina a violência velada do paternalismo brasileiro (onde "ser tratado como da família" é apenas uma máscara polida para a servidão moderna), transformando o espaço doméstico em um campo de batalha psicológico. Tirando um debate cultural de longa data dos seus trilhos narrativos mais comuns, a obra consegue lançar uma luz crua e implacável sobre as microagressões diárias e os ciclos de desigualdade que atravessam gerações. A direção de fotografia é surpreendentemente brilhante, com enquadramentos deliberados e potentes que mapeiam visualmente os distanciamentos emocionais e as fronteiras sociais dentro de uma mesma casa. As escolhas audiovisuais acertam ao conseguir transformar um ambiente doméstico e silencioso em uma arena de conflito visualmente marcante e instigante. A todo momento, a narrativa desfere golpes discretos, mas ainda assim amargos, àqueles que compartilham da consciência de classe. O que mais me pegou, no entanto, foi uma compreensão silenciosa: Ouvir o menino perguntar "Que horas ela volta?" no início parece apenas um aceno inteligente ao título. Ouvir a mesmíssima pergunta vindo da própria filha da Val no final do filme me atingiu de forma elegante -- foi um susto junto à uma realização devastadora, tanto para o público quanto para a própria Val, nos lembrando do que foi sacrificado e por quem.

texto: To put things briefly, The Substance is a relatively sound film, although, it still comes with a fair share of issues. As films of this more thematic nature, and more broadly within the horror genre typically demand, you’re sort of supposed to just go with the plot, which I struggle with. It’s not necessarily poorly written, it’s just contrived, not implausibly, but I still feel the beats could’ve been better strung together. Speaking of themes, it touches primarily on our contemporary culture, our media, and on the treatment of women, particularly within the public sphere; although I do find that the film fails to boldly challenge our perception of these social facets, or issues. For example, the premise, alongside how the film is shot evidently wish to discuss the self-objectification of the individual, of which is intrinsically tied to social norms, and to capitalism; yet this is highly surface level, and largely visual, it isn't actually protested. Overall, it's quite straightforward in its messaging, quite literally infantilising a woman, and I don’t have any qualms with it, however, a bit of nuance, or development upon these themes would’ve made the piece a touch more grounding, connecting, perhaps it might’ve helped alleviate the disconnect created by the grotesque body horror. On that, yeah, uhm, the film excels in disgusting me, although, I expected as much and genuinely struggled to convince myself to watch it. More technically, I was pleased in that colour wasn’t shied away from, as is the case frequently in this genre, and in this era; and the camerawork was solid, if albeit a bit uninspired—I also found it notable that some shots were clearly added solely for the sake of evoking disgust, or discomfort, even if the details were irrelevant, most prominently in the opening scenes of the film.

texto: SFF2024 #7 (Closing Night Film) Spends a surprising amount of its third act riffing on extremely specific images from a not very well-regarded Doctor Who episode. This gets a lot of mileage out of its excellent concept, which allows for both lots of squeamishly fun body horror and plenty of (definitely unsubtle but undeniably worthwhile) social commentary about how we view women’s bodies culturally & the speed at which we tend to discard those on our screens once they reach a certain age. To her credit, Fargeat handles the topic deftly without resorting to the self-seriousness that trips up many a horror movie that sets out to say something about a specific issue, though I did feel at times that the film’s camp tone was keeping me at a slight ironic distance from the emotions of the characters. Said characters are brought to life nicely by the cast, though. I don’t think this is quite as much of a Demi Moore showcase as some of the Cannes critics hailed it as (by plot necessity, she’s off-screen for large chunks of the runtime), but it’s certainly bold, electric work from her. There’s a sequence where her character is overcome by body image-related insecurities while getting ready to go out, and it’s made as viscerally heartbreaking as it is by Moore’s excellent work. Margaret Qualley’s material is a bit more one-note but, as usual, she sells it on her screen presence alone (also, at the risk of proving the movie’s point, it must be said that she is quite hot). Dennis Quaid’s turn would be way too much in almost any other movie but it works for this one’s camp sledgehammer of an approach. Fargeat’s cooking with all the right ingredients here, but I think she undercuts herself with self-indulgence. There’s no real reason for this to be 140 minutes long; the concept could have easily made for a brilliant, punchy 90-minutes. By the third act, the movie just keeps piling hats onto hats in service of a gorefest that strays too far from the original allegory. It’s not that it isn’t a natural escalation of the conflict, per se, but I think it’s possible to escalate things a little too much, to the point where it becomes more numbing than impactful. There were several great possible endings in the climax, but Fargeat just kept dragging it out for no apparent reason, and the whole movie - while never boring - is similarly just a bit flabby given the simplicity of its plot. The film’s issues are not big enough to entirely sink it, but they definitely made me feel a bit out of step with the hype from Cannes. As recent Cannes-awarded, women-directed body horrors go, I’m much more of a Titane man.

texto: Horrifying, stylish and clearly true to its intentions, The Substance is probably not for most, but you can’t deny it does what it does well. Unapologetically over the top, unsettling, gut-renching and excessive. At times it felt like never ending stimulation which was often overwhelming. Its strong Sci-fi element is enhanced by interesting designs and is complimented by a very well fitting score and visual aesthetic. All male characters were either hedonistic pigs or lame simps, the latter pretty much always being intolerable, though to its credit added to the unpleasantness of the world. Hyper-sexualisation served its underlying messages and aesthetic, however for me was excessive, although this perspective somewhat changed when I realised how exaggerated the rest movie was also. Denis Quade killed it. While I won’t be watching again, fans of body horror will surely be pleased, as this one takes the genre to new places in the craziest of ways. Well done, Coralie!

texto: honestly loved how everything is shoved into your face via visual presentation and cues. some might criticize how this film exaggerates the message, slapping it on you with direct transparency as if it isn’t obvious enough, but in a world full of films buried in subtext, it’s refreshing to see one that makes the message painfully clear—especially since men (both as individuals and as a system) still don’t systematically grasp how physically, socially, and mentally detrimental beauty standards are for women. SO HELL YEAH, SHOVE THE MESSAGE UP THEIR ASSES. even the male looksmaxxing culture is just the tip of the iceberg compared to women's trenches. the dynamic between demi and margaret is excellent, and i cannot stress enough how good the casting is. demi’s performance evoked so much empathy in me, especially in her self‑destructive moments and when she tried to bring sue back, which eventually led to her gory death. elisa’s childhood friend really stood out to me, as he's such a symbolic figure or reminder of her potential recovery and self‑acceptance, though we all knew how their date would end. i definitely caught the significance of the final act, but it didn’t stand out because it felt comical. technically, everything is excellent, but again, monstra elisasue comes across as more comical than anything. i may or may not have missed the subtext if that was intentional. ultimately, all i can say is i fucking love depictions of female insecurities and frustrations with mirrors as cinematic tools.

texto: This film is gonna be a huge divider. All I know is: I won't forget that screening in a hurry. Every Cannes has one: a love it or hate it title that becomes a word-of-mouth sensation thanks to the sheer division it creates among festivalgoers. No, we’re not talking about the so-bad-it-still-isn’t-good Megalopolis, but The Substance, a body horror that goes places even body horror aficionados will be shocked by. Helping this film’s cause are a few things – firstly, it’s the second film from Coralie Fargeat, whose gory thriller Revenge marked her out as one to watch back in 2017 – but, secondly it marks a return-of-sorts for 1990s icon Demi Moore, who is fantastically cast as an ageing Hollywood star who takes a black market drug to create a younger version of herself. The Substance is as gruesome as they come, culminating with an extended sequence that needs to be experienced with a crowd.

texto: Whoa!! This is awesome. Totally insane body horror of the highest order. Filled with the most gratuitously sexual shots of female bodies AND also the most disgustingly gross shots of [redacted] female bodies. It's entertaining as hell! Though the story isn't necessarily anything original (being obsessed with beauty always leads to misery) but the way it's told in THIS film is original. Horror fans are going to lose their shit for this. Rare to see the Cannes press screening audience go THIS wild during a film - that's always the mark of something truly great. If Coralie Fargeat could trim this down by 20 minutes and cut out some of the unnecessarily repetitive shots, this would be an all-timer. It's that close.

texto: Body horror goes crazyyyy! This movie does a great job representing the horrors of being a woman in Hollywood. The misogynistic urge to devalue a woman who ages naturally and the hyper unrealistic expectations for women to stay young, skinny and desirable is deeply disturbing. I think this was an important film for that reason and Demi and Margeret were both awesome here. I also LOVED the campiness- this movie doesn’t take itself too seriously. Would definitely recommend watching!

texto: La madre de Dios. Creo que es la primera vez que estoy enfadado de verdad después de ver una película. He gastado 3 horas (¡¡¡3 HORAS!!!) en ver el musical más plano, insulso y procedural que podría imaginarme. - Todas las canciones son iguales, es que no puedes recordar ni una sola de ellas nada más terminarla. Le preguntas a ChatGPT como serían las canciones de un musical de Harry Potter en el mundo de las golosinas y te saca todo el repertorio. - La estética es todo lo contrario a lo que me gusta (aunque lo esperaba). Vestuario y decorado Broadway saturado. Te vomitan colorines sin parar y a otra cosa mariposa. - El tono infantil de Disney pero llevado al extremo ridículo. Es una película para niños, si, pero sin ninguna pretensión de segunda capa o mensaje que lo tienen casi todas aunque sea mínimo. Fuera coñas al nivel de una serie procedural slop de Nickelodeon en 2010. - El ritmo hace que parezca que llevas viendo días la película, infinito tiempo gastado en ABSOLUTA NADA. Te cuentan 5 fun facts del origen del Mago de Oz en un milenio. La he parado unas 15 veces. 3 horas para esto y todavía queda la segunda parte, es que no me lo creo. Y sí, la voy a ver, lo que me faltaba era quedarme a medias después de tragarme la mitad de este plato chino sabor glutamato refrito. Si en la tv interdimensional esa de Rick&Morty hicieran una parodia de la industria del cine actual saldría exactamente esto. Ver buenos musicales me quitó el prejuicio que tenía sobre ellos y es que esto es todo lo que yo pensaba que eran cuando tenía 15 años y era un edgy anime gore.

texto: I struggle to call this a mixed bag because the good is not nearly as present in quantity as the bad. The film is a bit too comfortable with it's source material I think. It most consistently preforms when it is working as closely to the stage show as possible, i.e. the famously good music is still good. However it does not manage to overcome any of the flaws of the original product, nor I think, particularly thrill in it's limited ability to translate stage to film. Choreography and set design are both at best, adequate which is a shame for a product which should shine in both areas. Costuming is a bit better, but is kept down by the Netflix gray smudge color grading. How can you produce a film in Oz and not have any color! A world of bright shades is reduced to smudgy pinks, dull greens, and little else that is not seemingly grey or earth tone. The film is far worse for not having put in the work to be as delightful to look at as the original Oz film. The story is not very good, there is basically no modification from the stage show to my understanding, and the show has always coasted by on the musical numbers over the story. The same structure remains here, made worse by the fact this is only part one and several more hours of story remain. Overall a pretty unremarkable thing, it managed to never make me consider stopping watching, but not much beyond that in terms of impact.

texto: Wicked tells the story of Elphaba, a young woman born with green skin—an outcast due to her difference—who arrives at Shiz University. There, she meets Glinda, her polar opposite: popular, privileged, and deeply concerned with her image. Despite their differences, a genuine friendship forms between them as Elphaba gradually discovers that the world of Oz is far less wonderful than it appears. What I found interesting was the way the film questions who gets to decide what is "good" or "bad." Elphaba is rejected before she has even done anything, simply because she is different. Conversely, Glinda fits the mold of the "perfect" girl: beautiful, popular, and well-liked. Yet, as the story unfolds, this contrast becomes far less clear-cut. The relationship between the two is clearly one of the film’s highlights. They represent two completely different ways of responding to how others perceive them: Elphaba ultimately accepts rejection rather than compromising her convictions, whereas Glinda is far more invested in validation and popularity. Visually, I really enjoyed the world-building. Oz is incredibly colorful, intricately designed, and almost fairytale-like, featuring a striking contrast between Glinda’s bright, pink aesthetic and the darker tones associated with Elphaba. The costumes and sets give the film a strong identity, and the musical numbers are clearly designed as full-scale spectacles. However, despite all this, I felt the film sometimes lacked the depth it seemed to promise. While certain themes—such as discrimination and propaganda—are interesting, they remain somewhat simplistic. The film spends a great deal of time establishing its world and characters, which can make the story feel like it is moving rather slowly at times. The fact that this is only the first part of the story also reinforces this impression. We reach the end just as several plotlines are barely getting started. This is understandable, given that the film is designed as the first chapter, but as a standalone movie, I find it makes the experience less satisfying. Spoiler (ending): Elphaba finally discovers that the Wizard and Madame Morrible are manipulating events in Oz—specifically using the plight of the Animals to consolidate their power. She refuses to be part of this system and flees, while Glinda remains in Oz. Elphaba is then publicly branded a threat. However, the "Defying Gravity" scene is brilliantly executed; it perfectly captures Elphaba’s choice: she would rather be seen as wicked than conform to others' expectations of her. Ultimately, I found *Wicked* interesting and visually stunning, with excellent chemistry between the two female leads, yet I was left wanting a bit more regarding the story and the depth of certain themes. There was immense potential, but I was more impressed by the world-building and the spectacle than truly moved by the narrative itself.

texto: Best moment: “Defying gravity”. That song and scene is the centerpiece of the musical and this (and the other) movie. It doesn’t disappoint. The song by itself already feels epic but the movie version puts a cherry on top. This small action interlude on the broom is a fun little break before it works toward that climax and note we have all been waiting for. Best quote: “I don’t cause commotions. I am one.” MVP: Cynthia Erivo. First, her voice is stunning. It is so crystal clear and she switches between emotional to powerful with the flip of vocal cord. Second, the acting matches the vocal performance. She gives Elphaba so much heart and a deep compassion but that fury beneath the surface is always brewing. It is an emotional performance in all areas. Best visual: The wizard’s room. The rest of the movie is so bright, colorful and joyful. That set, however, is darker and there isn’t any of the joy of the Emerald City. The design of the big head also looks really cool and ominous. Best showstopper: “Dancing through life” is just so much fun. The part in the library has so much cool choreography with the books and the spinning set. The ballroom looks stunning and also has some fun choreography. In all of this I ask myself one important question: How can someone be as charming as Jonathan Bailey? Rating: 9 out of 10 flying monkeys

texto: M(a)y Korea Challenge 2025 38. SK Drama A completely superfluous remake of The Housemaid which is worse in every way. The maid gets a new backstory and Youn Yuh-jung, in her debut role, plays her as if "girl from the country" was a mental disorder. Less of a threatening sexual force she is just another broken trauma doll, infantile and ready to be abused. Overall, the menacing presence of female agency is replaced by brute masculine force (read: rape scenes, endowed with a giallo -esque visual flair). The "cautionary tale" framing narrative of the previous version, with its charmingly bizarre final scene, is traded for a clichéed police investigation. And since the children play no role at all, and simply disappear after a few early scenes, I even miss Ahn Sung-Ki's bratty antics. Nah; this was an unnecessary disappointment.

The scene didn’t quite translate to the main character story at all but seemed to be given a particular weight regardless.

texto: Myeong-ja convinced me to drink rat poison. I haven't seen The Housemaid by the same director and I think that's a bit of a problem as this is a heavily stylised and hysterically acted variation on the film he laid down over a decade earlier. Everything here has a melodrama turned up to the highest settings and the cast's performances become so flailing and ridiculous that you wonder if the film is insisting on not being taken seriously. What's more most of the cool stylisation is really front loaded and that's before the dialogue completely goes to crazy town so you're left with a first half that routinely looks really interesting and a tone which is off-kilter but not completely lost and then a second half where people are just having wild emotional swings and routinely falling in to complete hysteria in sets you've now seen a dozen times with lighting that can only be described as generic. The final sequence with two of the characters still manipulating future events whilst dying from having ingested rat poison did win me back a bit though. I'm still sat here having no clue what the film was even trying to do which makes critiquing it quite hard. Freya's rating: 1/5

texto: 《下女》裡傭人主動引誘金先生，敢於表達慾望、抽煙當壞女孩；《火女》裡則是主人借醉強暴傭人，鄉下女子來城市，願望是找個好老公，補完《下女》缺乏描述之處。仲介所樓梯是通往不同階層的道路。家庭是串連起整部電影的關鍵，女子要守清白之身，為日後要嫁人；出軌的丈夫一身臭味，婚外情性關係意味髒亂。暴露當日韓國社會保守。丈夫向妻子告白自己的出軌事跡，遭妻子唾棄，反指責妻子為何不能像其他人的妻子一樣放下瑣事，助丈夫發展事業。忍忍讓讓，都是為了維持中產家庭的運作。血案發生，纏糾結束。最後留下來面對悲劇的，還是已飽遭傷害的女性。尹汝貞處女作，不懂她在裡面演出是出於本意還是經過金綺泳調教，總整體而言，《火女》多有讓人浮誇失真。碎屍瘋癲，比《下女》多了幾分邪典的味道。

exemplo: Este grupo de reviews medianas aponta que o filme é essencialmente uma refilmagem do mesmo diretor, com estrutura narrativa muito similar, e que a comparação com a obra original é inevitável e, para muitos, desfavorável.
texto: I discovered by watching this that Woman of Fire that it's essentially a remake of The Housemaid , the last movie I watched. It's really strange that despite the controversy surrounding The Housemaid that they would remake it only ten years later. It's even stranger that after several wars and censorship implementations this would be one of the few surviving films left in Korean cinema. It's about 85 percent the same but it starts and ends differently. Our two female leads have a different and darker beginning from their counterparts in The Housemaid and there are a few different deaths along the way. In general I didn't like Woman of Fire as much. It feels cheap and, in some ways, lazily put together. The editing is all over the place, the version I watched had some bizarre subtitles, and I didn't feel that the performances were very strong. Overall, a short and side-tracking film that you can watch when feeling adventurous with your watchlist.

texto: Asian Cinema Challenge 2024: boxd.it/rgmNA 4. Korean Film Archive Top 100 Future Academy Award winner Youn Yuh-jung made her debut in Kim Ki-young's psychedelic remix/reworking/reshuffle (take your pick) of his superior 1960 film The Housemaid. With its Argento-esque colours and manic imagery, Woman of Fire has some subtle differences in approach to the monochrome melodrama The Housemaid. But I don't think this remake of sorts adds much to the original. Both are about sin, although the 1971 film cranks up the sultriness whereas the original pressed forth the dissolution of the family dynamic. But The Housemaid feels fresher and it cranks up the tension more gradually than the psychosexual Woman of Fire.

texto: «Женщина в огне» – первый авторемейк эпохальной «Горничной» Ким Ги-ёна (второй выйдет спустя одиннадцать лет), своеобразная ревизия общественных нравов, выполняемая режиссером раз в десятилетие. Для корейских кинематографистов «Hanyo» стала настольной библией, а ее сюжет стал бродячим, плотно войдя в кинематографический канон. Новая версия культовой картины, вошедшая в мизогиническую трилогию, очевидно, снята под большим влиянием джалло, в отличие от строгого по форме черно-белого оригинала первый авторемейк изобилует всеми оттенками взрывных красного и синего, а квартирные интерьеры становятся объектом эстетизации. Ким Ги-ён или как его прозвали на родине «господин Монстр» выходит на пик своей творческой формы, снимая предельно экзальтированные картины, смешивающие особенности корейского менталитета, насилие, разрушение семьи, сексуальные девиации, женобоязнь и дикие сюрреалистические образы. В «Hwanyeo» режиссер немного отходит в сторону от социальных аллегорий оригинала, делая акцент на психологической подоплеке поступков героев – они идут вразнос, чтобы постепенно сойти с ума. С наступлением Четвертой республики в стране уже установилась цензура, поэтому кореец выбирает самое надежное укрытие – в глубине жанровых картин, но его персонажи по-прежнему зловещи и пугающи, балансируя на грани откровенной карикатуры и звериной монструозности. Дебютантка Юн Ё-Дзён, сыгравшая коварную деревенскую простушку, открыла галерею чудовищ в женском обличье в самом ярком творческом десятилетии режиссера, но в отличие от злодейки из первого фильма, поступки героини, выбравшей проторить себе путь наверх по социальной лестнице, обоснованы ненавистью в сторону мира мужчин, уже жестоко обошедшегося с девушкой. Ким Ги-ён вставляет в самые кульминационные моменты звук удара по раскаленному железу (постоянно напоминающий героине о чудовищном моменте из прошлого), вместе с кислотной цветовой палитрой и чередой взрывных экспрессионистских образов они окаймляют психологические перверсии, разрушающие шаткий мир корейской семьи, свято чтящей патриархат и встроенной в жесткое капиталистическое общество. Колесо смерти набирает обороты, руки героев окрашиваются кровью, безумие уже замерло на пороге. Новая версия классовой «Служанки» мутирует в психоделическую мелодраму о женщинах и мужчинах на грани нервного срыва, незваная гостья, обуреваемая стыдом и желанием, преследуемая психологической травмой, срывает маски с благопристойных членов корейского общества, как огня боящихся разоблачения и потери статуса. Если в оригинале Ким Ги-ён выводил на экране кровожадных паучих, рвущих мужчину на части, чтобы сделать его марионеткой в своих руках, то в «Женщина в огне» превращает героиню в разносящую по дому заразу крысу, искажая внутренний мир хозяев дома, забывающих о всех моральных ценностях и превращающихся в зверей. В картине есть как грех, так и искупление, как похоть, так и невинность, как отчаяние, так и смирение. Но благообразная маска успешной семьи, чей социальный капитал гораздо важнее любви и преданности, уже треснула, поэтому вой оставшейся в живых перебивает звон ненавистного металла. Грязное, извращенное и одновременно притягивающее к себе зрелище.

texto: 🇰🇷March is Korea Month🇰🇵 One of those curious instances where a director remade his own previous film. In this case, Kim Ki-young redoes his seminal potboiler “ The Housemaid ” in color with a few minor plot tweaks and a bit more experimental editing. We see more of the housemaid’s perspective this time, where her actions are informed by a traumatic past while living in the country. She and a friend move to the city to start fresh only for her to get romantically involved with the husband of the family she serves. Youn Yuh-jung delivers an off kilter performance that occasionally comes across like camp, where she seems to be trying too hard to play crazy. The color is noticeable enough to seemingly justify the remake from a visual perspective, but I kept pining for the starkness of the original’s black and white. Overall I just preferred the original, especially since this broadly just felt like the same movie again, but it hits the beats needed to tell the story decently. A warning for those interested, the version that’s streaming on Tubi has a weird blurring at the bottom of the screen during every line of dialogue, and the whole image is noticeably cropped. I have to assume this print originally had burned in subtitles, and someone did some digital work to try and remove them. Also the subtitles that were provided are humorous in their descriptive quality. Early on there’s a flashback, and it’s accompanied by the subtitle “she remembers her past.” Three and a half stars.

texto: Kim Ki-young's Housemaid (1961) frequently has "best Korean film" praise thrown at it - a predecessor to the erotic thriller, about the title character bringing a family to ruin.  The runaway success meant that Kim would revisit the collateral damage of extramarital affairs for a "Housemaid Trilogy" - while making a number of other efforts in a very similar vein (i.e. Insect Woman).  Woman of Fire (1971) is the second film in the trilogy, and features Oscar winner Youn Yuh-jung (Minari) in her feature film debut, as our femme fatale homewrecker.  This is not a spiritual sequel, but rather the director remaking his work a decade later. Woman of Fire streamlines the narrative, cutting down on the family dynamic, now primarily taking the perspective of the Housemaid.  The children are non-characters, which removes a vulnerability that drove the originals abstract terror, and made it so perversely compelling.  Instead the extra minutes not dedicated to similar beats and exactly the same dialogue, have a more elaborate blackmail set-up, and three sexual assaults.  It's rougher and more graphic, sadly losing the cerebral aspects that made the original so steeped in dread & unique.  The decision to revisit the work in decade cycles, is an interesting one - as the world has changed drastically in ten years.  A big part of the 1961 situation was economic factors forcing the nuclear family into an impossible situation, here the threat of financial ruin no longer holds sway - and ease with which the husband is seduced makes him comedically buffoonish.  The architecture of the house is delightful, with sharp features inviting the Dutch camera angles that follow.  Now in colour, with Kim making the most of them - frequently saturate the image in reds and blues that lend themselves to the fever dream asthetic.  Experimental editing abounds, with the death of an infant handled in a tasteful succession of still images.  While the narrative asks less of the audience, and characters, it is still grounded in two powerhouse performances by Youn, and Jeon Gye-hyeon as the wife. Worth seeking out, and I would strongly encourage viewing it as a double bill with the original for insights into the changing times, and evolution of the artists' choices in a much stricter environment. South Korea Marathon

tema: Comparação com a obra original de 1960
exemplo: Muitas reviews positivas comparam este filme com a versão original de 1960, notando que, embora seja uma refilmagem da mesma história pelo mesmo diretor, esta versão traz cores vibrantes, mais caos e uma abordagem mais ousada, embora algumas prefiram a tensão do original em preto e branco.
texto: A remake/retelling of Kim's own film, The Housemaid (1960). Whereas the earlier movie addresses the concerns of creeping materialism into Korean society in the aftermath of the war, Woman of Fire uses the same narrative to plot a more sexually-charged tale focusing on the exploitation and subjugation of women in a highly conservative and patriarchal society. Woman of Fire is a gripping and evocative story which focuses on bodily autonomy, inter-relation power dynamics and violence towards women which, sadly, still feels rather topical even whilst watching this in 2020. Mixing elements of horror and melodrama, this is a highly engaging movie which (alongside Kim's other films) have had a clear and deep impact on modern Korean cinema - watching this, we can see the direct influence it had on Bong Joon-ho's Parasite. It is a deep shame that Kim Ki-yong's films have yet to find themselves included in the established canon of popular world cinema but, with Parasite providing a belated breakthrough for Korean cinema onto the world stage, belated recognition for one of the most unique voices in movie history is a distinct possibility.

Youn Yuh-Jung is so entertaining in her debut it’s no wonder that she is recognized with an Oscar. Since the 60s was a Golden Age of Cinema then the 70s was Darkness — Korea’s government dominated and repressed what could be released into media. I’m surprised and grateful to watch some crazy shit that happens in this movie. What happens when you restrain creativity? It needs a release.

texto: Unhinged? CHECK! Entertaining? YES! Logical? NOT SO MUCH. I found this updating of THE HOUSEMAID to be overlong and a bit too hysterical, but it's still fun. Nothing that anybody does makes much sense in a modern context, and it's hard to accept that there was a time, place or culture in which people would behave in such a ridiculous way. A young country girl, traumatized by an attack by a would-be rapist that she ends up murdering, moves to the big city to take work as a housemaid. Rather than be paid, she asks only that the woman of the house find her a husband. Unfortunately, the 1st man she meets after her employment starts is her employers husband. And though he insists over and over and over again to anyone who might care that he extremely proud of having never cheated on his wife, if he gets drunk all bets are off. Youn Yuh-jung's odd performance as the mad girl who is continually re-traumatized was her film acting debut. 50 years later she would win an Academy Award (Best Performance by an Actress in a Supporting Role) as the granny in MINARI. I am so looking forward to seeing her in the new season of BEEF.

exemplo: O filme é descrito como histérico, absurdo e delirante, com reviravoltas extremas e uma espiral de loucura que, embora possa parecer excessiva, mantém o interesse pela sua ousadia.
texto: Woman of Fire , the second film in Kim Ki-Young’s “Housemaid Trilogy," is an interesting variation on Kim’s exceptional classic The Housemaid that's dominated by explosive colors (red and blue especially), aggressive camerawork, sexual acts obscured and spliced with suggestive photomontages thanks to censorship, and over-the-top acting. Similar to the original, this remake centers a love triangle (or "eternal triangle") between a middle class married couple and a housemaid, who is a country bumpkin this time around. Having now seen this, I'm of the belief that, in addition to the original, it also influenced 2010's The Housemaid . I appreciate the focus on class and gender dynamics as well as the central theme of "contamination" as the protagonists become corrupted and steadily deviate from their moral values as the narrative unfurls. I also like the reoccurring use of the need/desperation for water, which can be interpreted as a metaphor for a desire for "purification." This film trades in nuance and narrative substance for being exaggerated, absurd, and stylish - this isn't necessarily a bad thing, I'm just stating a fact; it works for what Kim is trying to accomplish. It's also more "seedy" and depraved than the original, but not in a way that makes it better or worse than the original - I just see it as another more modernized, differentiating aspect of this reimagining of the lurid housemaid tale. While not on par with the original (IMO), Woman of Fire is certainly a spicy, twisted, and entertaining psychosexual melodrama. 🌟 Why I Love East Asian Cinema 🌟

texto: I have the two other versions (60 and 82) too far away in my memory to be able to compare them reliably, I can only say that it is a curious cinematographic exercise by Kim Ki-young and both three are fascinating in their own style. In this case, even though the spiral of madness begins very early, the picture never stops increasing  insanity and sordidness in a way that is as formally stylized through sets,sound and cinematography as it is distressing thanks to the violently overdramatic excess in each character, way ahead of its time. It is not an easy movie to find but if you can read French, it is available on YouTube and despite not being the best quality, it is worth it..

The psychedelic imagery didn’t really do it for me personally, but was a unique touch. The altered story felt less real but allows Myeong-Ja to develop into an arguably more compelling femme fatale. Overall, I prefer the original, but this one is still enjoyable.

texto: Kim Ki Young remade his seminal work, The Housemaid, not just once but twice! Woman of Fire was his second bite at the apple. It's wild! Youn Yuh-jung in her debut role plays a crazed country bumpkin turned housemaid. It's a physical role. She is expressive and at times kind of scary. Film at Lincoln Center screened an old print of this hard-to-find movie that had huge French subtitles they couldn't get rid of. the French title is more apt, Woman of Satan, implying that her behavior is attributable to demonic possession. Yes, it's that insane. The film series opened with a pre recorded intro by Park Chan-wook in which he explains the influence these 70s Korean movies had on his own artistry. And you can see the influence. The fascination with class relations, the dark comedy, the off-kilter characters, the willingness to take things to the extreme. I loved the bright colors they were able to preserve on this print. The dubbing is almost comically bad; not sure if that is the print quality or just the style. And I liked the clever montages of slides to get around the censors, accompanied by gunshot sounds in an almost Godardian homage. I could imagine this being remade without the censors in a much more graphic and explicitly deranged way.
